articles.title: Sonora Rally Evolves for 2027 with Three-Day Format And Rally Schools
articles.summary: Route planning for adventure motorcycles sits right between logistics and art. A good route doesn’t just connect points on a map—it shapes the entire experience, manages your risk, and determines whether a trip becomes a highlight reel or an expensive recovery story. In this episode of our ADV 101 series, we break down how to plan sustainable, epic backcountry adventure rides. From calculating true "time to traverse" instead of relying on mileage to land access regulations, weather extremes, bailout options, and using paper maps alongside GPS tools like Gaia, onX, and Garmin Tread. Check out the written article here: https://www.motorcycle.com/bikes/how-to/adv-101-the-art-of-route-planning-44668846 Thanks to Yamaha Motor Corporation USA for sponsoring this video. Learn more at www.yamahamotorsports.com For 2025, Aprilia didn't reinvent the wheel — they refined the standard 659cc parallel-twin with Euro 5+ compliance and punchier low-gear fueling. Then, they dropped the Rally Edition: a package that's ready to rock equipped with factory armor, narrower tubeless wheels, a titanium SC-Project exhaust, and linear-rate KYB fork springs. We put the Aprilia Tuareg Rally through its paces to see if the $1,500 factory upgrade is worth your hard-earned cash.
articles.body:
The Sonora Rally is hoping to make it easier for new riders and racers to take part in the event.

Sonora Rally Evolves for 2027 with a New Three-Day Format and Expanded Rally Schools Built for Everyone from First-Time Navigators to Dakar-Bound Racers

For 13 years, Sonora Rally has given competitors a place to discover what rally raid really demands. Navigation. Endurance. Independence. A roadbook, an odometer, a machine, and enough open desert to find out whether all four-and the person behind the wheel or handlebars-can work together. Now, in 2027, Sonora Rally is making that experience easier to reach without making the rally itself easy.

The 2027 Sonora Rally, February 11–14, introduces a streamlined three-day rally raid based from a single bivouac in the San Luis Río Colorado region of Sonora, Mexico. Competitors unpack once, establish one home base, and race from there-reducing the expense, time, and moving logistics traditionally associated with rally raid while preserving the navigation, terrain, competition, and adventure that have defined Sonora for more than a decade. It is, quite simply, fewer logistics and more rally.

Just south of the U.S.–Mexico border, San Luis Río Colorado also puts the event within easy reach of competitors traveling from the United States, Canada, and Mexico. International racers can connect through San Diego, Phoenix, Mexicali, or Mexico City, while Fly-N-Race Moto and UTV rental and support programs offer another option for competitors who would rather arrive ready to race than haul an entire program across the continent.

And before February ever arrives, Sonora is opening the desert for something else: learning how to race it.

The Sonora Rally Schools return December 4–6, 2026, with an expanded format designed around a simple reality: not everyone who comes to Sonora needs the same training.

For Baja racers, desert riders, UTV competitors, and newcomers curious about making the jump into rally raid, the Navigation School combines classroom instruction with practical dune navigation. It offers first-timers a foundation in roadbook racing while giving developing competitors the opportunity to sharpen their navigation before returning to race Sonora in February.

Learn navigation in December. Race Sonora in February.

For experienced rally racers and Dakar-bound competitors, the Advanced Route removes the classroom altogether. Challenging Dakar-style roadbooks put the emphasis on seat time, navigation, and training in the dunes-a chance to prepare for Dakar or sharpen the tools required for Sonora 2027.

This year also introduces an entirely new option: a one-day Dunes Clinic led by ZXMoto Joyride Factory rider, multi-year Dakar veteran and former Sonora Rally Road to Dakar winner Skyler Howes, alongside Sonora Rally organizer and Dakar veteran Darren Skilton.

Limited to only eight vehicles, the clinic offers a focused day of hands-on big-dune training ahead of the weekend schools. For competitors accustomed to speed but less accustomed to reading large dunes, momentum and terrain, it offers an opportunity to learn from two people whose experience was earned in precisely those environments.

The objective across all three programs is not to make rally raid simple. It is to make learning it more accessible.

The rally may be shorter in 2027. The opportunity is not.

As North America's only official Road to Dakar event, Sonora Rally continues to offer competitors a pathway toward the sport's biggest stage.

In the UTV Road to Dakar, the winning eligible team will receive a paid entry into the 2028 Dakar Rally, a prize valued at more than $33,000 USD.*

For motorcycles, eligible competitors who finish the 2027 Sonora Rally will earn six Dakar eligibility points toward Dakar 2028.*

The new format therefore changes the commitment required to reach the starting line-not what waits on the other side of it.

From a first roadbook to a Dakar campaign, Sonora Rally is building a clearer path into rally raid. Come to learn. Come to train. Come to race. And for those with considerably bigger ideas, come find out where the roadbook can take you.

Dunes Clinic • Navigation School • Advanced Training

2027 SONORA RALLY - THREE-DAY RALLY RAID

Special incentives available for the first 20 entries.

articles.title: Fantasy Football Rankings: Hayden Winks' WR Blueprint for Week 6
articles.summary: Fantasy football analyst Hayden Winks shares the Blueprint to the WR position for Week 5.
articles.body:
The Blueprint is my weekly column and basically everything that I use to build out the most accurate rankings I can. There will be an RB column , this WR column on Thursdays and a combination column on the onesie positions . You will find film notes and endless charts. Maybe enough charts to stress test the Yahoo website. I kid.

It's impossible to get every ranking thoroughly early in the week, so be sure to keep checking in on these columns through Sunday morning. As always, my full rankings at every position are available .

1. Puka Nacua (vs. BUF) - 92.5 proj. receiving yards

Nacua's "pre-hernia" injury could be a serious long-term issue, but while he's in the lineup, he has the best projection every week. He got the best of an impressive Eagles secondary last week (WR5 on WR7 usage) while re-entering the lineup, and this matchup is far easier. The Rams have a monster 28.75-point team total (third) while hosting the Bills on Monday Night Football. Buffalo has allowed the third-most fantasy points to WRs this year, including a 2-TD game from Romeo Doubs (WR8) on top of big games from Amon-Ra St. Brown (WR4) and Nico Collins (WR9). They've missed CB1 Christian Benford recently, and the size issue from CB2 Maxwell Hairston will be one the Rams will certainly target here. They've allowed five TDs on just 27 man coverage reps this year.

2. Amon-Ra St. Brown (at ARI) - 79.5 proj. receiving yards

St. Brown is the WR5 on WR1 overall usage this season. His 11.5 targets per game keep him on pace for 196 targets this year. Dating back to last year, St. Brown has cleared 14.2 expected half PPR points in eight straight games with the Lions' secondary falling apart.

The Lions project for a league-high 30.0 points this week against a sorry Cardinals defense. They've allowed the fourth-most fantasy points to WRs so far, including top-17 finishes to Malik Nabers (WR10), Deebo Samuel (WR17), Jaxon Smith-Njigba (WR1) and Ladd McConkey (WR11). It's go time.

3. Jaxon Smith-Njigba (vs. SF) - 89.5 proj. receiving yards

JSN drafters on Yahoo have won 62% of their games, the highest of any WR through four weeks. He's the WR1 overall on WR3 overall usage, averaging a ridiculous 120 YPG on 10.3 targets.

Smith-Njigba faced the 49ers five times since 2024, scoring 7.8, 9.4, 11.4, 14.9, and 16.8 half PPR points in them. He's only scored a touchdown once in them while clearing 84 yards in 3 of 5. They've played him well all things considered, but their lack of pass rush right now works in JSN's favor. The Seahawks are at home with a 24.25-point team total (ninth). The 49ers gave up a score to Jaylen Waddle last week and Michael Wilson finished as the WR4 overall the week prior. It's a totally fine matchup for JSN.

4. CeeDee Lamb (vs. TB) - 79.5 proj. receiving yards

Lamb has 25 receiving first downs this year, only trailing 2011 Wes Welker for the most in NFL history through four weeks. He's shredded the Ravens and Texans defenses most recently, too. Lamb played a season-high 38% snaps in the slot to get away from CB1 Derek Stingley, including on his game-winning in-cut versus safety Jalen Pitre. It's a well-coached offense with quality protection and elite skill players. Dallas will compete for the scoring title. Lamb is the WR2 on WR4 usage so far, leading in receptions (9.3 per game) and yards (125 per game).

The blitz-heavy Bucs can catch bad OLs and QBs by surprise, but Prescott is amongst the best against the blitz over years of data. Lamb can be a quick outlet, as he was last week, but he can also get downfield where the Bucs have been exposed by Jordan Addison (WR10) and Denzel Boston (WR11) recently. Dallas has a 29.0-point team total (second).

5. Drake London (vs. BAL) - 89.5 proj. receiving yards

In 14 games with Michael Penix Jr. since 2024, London is now the WR3 (17.2 half PPR points) on WR8 usage (15.8 expected), WR1 overall target share (35%) and WR1 overall air yards (116 per game). He's finished as the WR2 overall and the WR24 overall (without a TD) in his two games with him this year. Penix has executed his under-center play action reps and is moving just enough to have a productive season. Penix wants to drive the ball, and London is running more deep breaking routes in this offense to fit in. There will be some underneath work, but London could be a killer on intermediate throws. Penix had an awesome anticipation throw before a zone defender had time to make a play on the ball on a corner route last night. London has an obvious case to be an early Round 2 pick if drafting today.

The Ravens have a good defense, but they are still working out the kinks and don't have an overpowering pass-rushing unit in general. They've allowed the eighth-most fantasy points to WRs so far, including a career-high 145 yards to Carnell Tate last week. CeeDee Lamb (WR13) and Chris Olave (WR9) had their usual games against them as clear-cut top targets. Atlanta has a 23.25-point team total (12th) at home.

6. Nico Collins (at TEN) - 79.5 proj. receiving yards

Collins is the WR3 on WR5 usage this season, averaging 9.0 targets per game as one of the most dominant players on tape. There is no competition for targets in Houston with its run game in shambles once again; it'd make sense to start leaning into the pass game more than ever. CJ Stroud is playing well.

The matchup is also a solid one. Houston has a 23.0-point team total (13th) in Tennessee, and its defense is far more dominant at DT than anywhere else right now. Teams should be comfortable passing against them in neutral situations. I've seen DeVonta Smith (WR6), Dontayvion Wicks (WR27) and Zay Flowers (WR6) give them major trouble this year. CB1 Alontae Taylor and CB2 Cor'Dale Flott are players to target as mismatches for Collins' size and speed. He has 79+ yards or a TD in all five career games against the Titans, including a WR4 overall finish in Week 11 last season.

7. Michael Wilson (vs. DET) - 72.5 proj. receiving yards

Wilson has some of the best WR tape of 2026. He's a great route runner at the top of his break, he's physical and he has moments at the catch point. His third-and-1 deep out route last week was sensational stuff. Down six points with seconds remaining at the 5-yard line, Wilson was targeted on first-, second- and fourth-down. Were they completed? No, but that's a great sign that he's trusted down there.

Through four weeks, Wilson is the WR22 on WR6 usage. Since Week 11 of last year, Wilson only trails Puka Nacua, Jaxon Smith-Njigba, Chris Olave and Amon-Ra St. Brown in fantasy points per game (15.5). He's WR2 in air yards per game and WR3 in targets per game during that stretch, too. I think he's far more of a fantasy WR2 than the market believes.

The matchup is the best one in the NFL. WR rooms facing the Lions are averaging 56 more yards per game against them compared to the rest of their schedule right now, easily the most in the NFL. They desperately miss S Brian Branch (Achilles) and other starting CBs, and they're put in tough spots because the Lions offense is scoring at will. Just look at Tetairoa McMillan (WR1 overall), Garrett Wilson (WR3) and Chris Olave (WR6 without a TD) versus the Lions. The Cardinals project for 24.5 points at home, while the Lions have a league-leading 30.0 total. Get excited.

8. Davante Adams (vs. BUF) - 62.5 proj. receiving yards

Adams is the WR16 on WR6 usage in 18 games with Puka Nacua since last year. He busted last week after multiple fingertip missed plays for explosives and touchdowns, but the underlying numbers were otherwise there with WR10 expected points (15.6) and nine targets. Nacua is a baller still but also maybe a step slower while playing with this "pre-hernia" injury, and Adams is moving quite well on tape right now.

The matchup with the Bills is tasty. It's at home with extra rest on Monday Night Football, and they've been shredded by physical WRs this year, especially without CB1 Christian Benford. Romeo Doubs (WR8) and Efton Chism III had SportsCenter moments last week, while Amon-Ra St. Brown (WR4) and Nico Collins (WR9) did their thing in previous outings. A 28.75-point team total (third) is the final obvious tell to start Adams as an upside WR1/2.

Jefferson (ankle) expects to play after missing last week with a low-ankle sprain, even with the Vikings having a bye next week. They'd only let him play if he was truly ready to go given that context. I'm not docking him for injury. Jordan Addison is also dealing with a hamstring injury, though he was back at practice Thursday.

10. Chris Olave (vs. MIN) - 79.5 proj. receiving yards

Olave has a seven-game streak of 15+ half PPR points and 14+ expected half PPR points. He's the WR6 overall on WR2 usage this year with Tyler Shough comfortably leading the NFL in dropbacks. He'd be an early Round 2 pick if redrafting today.

The Vikings will easily be the toughest test yet, especially with LT Kelvin Banks Jr. (IR) being replaced by an inexperienced player who is allowing a near league-high rate of pressures. That gets turned up against DC Brian Flores, who is as good as anyone in league history at destroying protection rules. They also play with two deep safeties often, so it's a bit harder to find the explosive plays that have made Olave one of the best fantasy WRs in the game. Minnesota has allowed the 19th-most fantasy points to WRs, largely driven by a massive downfield outing from Christian Watson (WR2) in Week 1. They haven't allowed a top-30 fantasy WR since then versus the Dolphins, Bucs and Bears. The Saints project for 19.5 points (22nd), far fewer than normal.

11. Garrett Wilson (vs. CLE) - 69.5 proj. receiving yards

Wilson was rug-pulled by a Jets outing that resulted in the fourth-fewest plays (32) in a single game in NFL history. The Bears also did a good job of limiting Wilson on their dropbacks, but that will go down as an outlier game. Wilson was the WR15 on WR25 usage and the WR3 on WR9 usage in the previous two outings with Breece Hall (quad), AD Mitchell (finger) and Mason Taylor (thumb) all sidelined. They're all still injured, so Wilson's ceiling is far higher than usual.

The Browns are the only team in the NFL actually playing man coverage at a notable rate. They've used it 88 times. The next closest is at 57, by the Patriots. They can do it because CB1 Denzel Ward is having another great season, and they are enjoying a great season from S Ronnie Hickman. This will be a "ball up top" matchup. The Jets are projected for 21.0 points (21st) while at home.

12. George Pickens (vs. TB) - 69.5 proj. receiving yards

Pickens is the most obvious buy-low ever. He's only the WR39 on WR23 usage this season, but the tape is showing plenty of DPIs called on him and some bad luck. There will be huge games coming with the Cowboys already leading the NFL in points per drive (3.4) without star LG Tyler Smith, who returns for Thursday Night Football. Dating back to last year, Pickens is the WR17 on WR12 usage with 22% of the targets in games with CeeDee Lamb.

The Cowboys are projected for the second-most points at home against an 0-4 Bucs team. This historically is a pass-funnel defense, and the Todd Bowles blitzes aren't going to catch Dak Prescott by surprise as much as they've worked against lesser offenses. Splash plays from Jordan Addison (WR10) and Denzel Boston (WR11) are reasons for upside WR2 faith. We can panic if Pickens doesn't come through tonight ...

13. Christian Watson (vs. CHI) - 59.5 proj. receiving yards

Watson had his worst game of the year last week, but nothing has materially changed other than Tucker Kraft is becoming more involved after a horrible start to his season coming off a torn ACL. That could hurt Watson at the margins, especially when (if) Josh Jacobs returns. Watson is still the WR8 on WR12 usage and WR14 targets per game (7.8).

A matchup with the Bears may be a little more difficult than it seemed pre-season after DC Dennis Allen has gotten the most of his injured defense, but it's still a fun game to target. Jalen Coker had a WR1 overall finish against them in Week 1, for crying out loud. The Packers are projected for 22.0 points (16th) as slight home dogs. Watson had three games against the Bears last year; 36 yards with a score in the playoff loss, a 17-yard dud in Week 16 and a WR5 overall finish in Week 14.

14. Matthew Golden (vs. CHI) - 59.5 proj. receiving yards

Golden is the WR17 on WR10 usage and WR9 targets per game (9.0) this season, with 10+ half PPR points and 10+ expected half PPR points in 3-of-4 contests. He's been a more explosive version of the Romeo Doubs role from last year, but now there's not a No. 3 receiver to get "gimme" looks. Those can trickle down to Golden, too.

See more about the matchup in the Christian Watson blurb from above, noting the primary difference is Golden's matchup with CB2 Tyrique Stevenson is far better than against CB1 Jaylon Johnson.

15. Zay Flowers (at ATL) - 69.5 proj. receiving yards

Flowers is not expected to have Lamar Jackson this time around, which obviously impacts his efficiency a ton, but OC Declan Doyle is very reliant on Flowers being the focal point of the pass game. He's being used underneath in ways that should keep his floor high with Tyler Huntley at QB. His yards per route being in his own stratosphere is helpful when readjusting for his new situation. He's the WR6 on WR15 usage, including two half-games.

The matchup is a strong one, too. The Falcons are well coached but down CB1 A.J. Terrell and two impact pass rushers. They've allowed the fourth-most passing yards per game (277) and seventh-most fantasy points to WRs so far. Chris Olave (116 yards), Christian Watson (96 yards) and Tetairoa McMillan (101 yards) all have been excellent as the top targets in their offenses against them recently. Baltimore's 20.25-point team total is just about seven points less than normal, and Derrick Henry's has a disproportionate touchdown share in this offense.

16. Malik Nabers (at WAS) - 59.5 proj. receiving yards

Update: Nabers (knee) had soreness on Wednesday and missed practice, but returned on Thursday.

Hand up — I got this one way wrong last week when I ranked him closer to the WR3 range. Nabers was the WR10 on WR30 usage with multiple explosives. He beat a heavy-footed LB on a seam ball for a TD, high-pointed a lollipop from Jameis Winston on a deep corner route and had a great circus route with massive separation. There was some underneath success, too, including a hitch route that led to two broken tackles. We're inching closer to 90% health as we head into October, and with the Giants at 3-1, it'll likely be Jameis for the near future. Nabers is trending upwards as the WR33 on WR38 usage this season.

The matchup is a great one. The Commanders are doing the chaos at the line of scrimmage thing a lot more than others with new DC Daronte Jones (from the Brian Flores tree), and it's funneled a lot more yards via the air (eighth-most) than on the ground (27th). Star WRs have had big outings against them already; JSN (WR1 overall) and CeeDee Lamb (WR3 overall). There's no reason to believe in Mike Sainristill in boundary coverage right now. The Giants project for 19.0 points (26th), however and it will almost always be a fairly run-heavy plan under Harbaugh.

17. Parker Washington (vs. PHI) - 59.5 proj. receiving yards

18. Jaylen Waddle (at LAC) - 59.5 proj. receiving yards

Waddle's season-long ceiling isn't hitting as we'd hoped. His 21% target share and WR37 expected half PPR points sit too far down to be trusted as more than an inconsistent WR2/3 in fantasy. Bo Nix's quick trigger to the checkdown has left some potential intermediate and downfield throws on the field, and the Sean Payton offense will always have schemed up targets to others. Waddle did have two screen receptions in Week 4, and his overall involvement could tick up with valued WR3 Pat Bryant (IR, ankle) now injured. Waddle has also dropped a couple of passes for potential explosives this year to tilt us further. He's the WR32 per game. I'm waiting for the 50-yard YAC moment ...

19. Jameson Williams (at ARI) - 49.5 proj. receiving yards

Dud-dud-dud-boom. That's the story with Jamo. He had three comeback receptions, one screen, one quick out and one go ball Cover 3 hole shot heading into halftime in a wild loss to the Panthers. His day could've been bigger had he come down with two designed chunk plays (double move down the sideline and bootleg play-action dig). Williams ultimately finished WR19 on WR20 usage without scoring a touchdown, and the fact that the Lions defense yet again couldn't get stops bodes well for Williams' WR3 odds this year. He's been the WR45 on WR33 usage this season as a positive regression candidate.

20. DK Metcalf (vs. IND) - 49.5 proj. receiving yards

21. Josh Downs (at PIT) - 59.5 proj. receiving yards

22. Mike Evans (at SEA) - 49.5 proj. receiving yards

23. Romeo Doubs (vs. LV) - 49.5 proj. receiving yards

Doubs has been the wildest rollercoaster of the year, but Week 4 was nothing but a total smash. Aside from an extremely low ball that was tossed by Doubs into the air for an INT, Doubs played well. He had a skinny post TD, a 4th-and-3 slant win and a one-handed fade TD. His WR8 finish was on WR11 expected half PPR points, and the Patriots also lost Mack Hollins (calf) around halftime. They're running out of bodies for Drake Maye to throw to, so Doubs' value is absolutely trending up. His expected half PPR points have climbed every week: 2.6, 5.2, 6.7, 15.4.

25. Luther Burden III (at GB) - 49.5 proj. receiving yards

26. Rome Odunze (at GB) - 39.5 proj. receiving yards

27. Carnell Tate (vs. HOU) - 49.5 proj. receiving yards

Tate had a career-high 15.8 expected half PPR points in Week 4 and his usage has climbed in three straight games. Results were mixed, but things are generally trending up. Cam Ward delivered a couple of wow throws out of structure to Tate, who was only targeted five+ yards downfield on all 12 of his looks. There were some high throws with offbeat timing in there, but the volume is real and there will be go-ball explosives eventually. He had a double-move penalty drawn on him from All-Pro S Kyle Hamilton as an example. Tate is the WR34 on WR22 usage to start his career, and I don't see Calvin Ridley, Wan'Dale Robinson and others eating into his alpha status.

This assumes Ja'Marr Chase (concussion) and Tee Higgins (adductor) are out. More later.

Diggs (hamstring) did not practice on Wednesday. More later.

30. Devaughn Vele (vs. MIN) - 39.5 proj. receiving yards

Vele is a real fantasy WR3. He became a full-time player in Week 12 last year, and he's the WR22 on WR17 usage in eight games since. This year, Vele is the WR21 on WR13 usage with Tyler Shough leading the NFL with 48 dropbacks per game. Only six other teams are above 40 for reference.

Vele's extreme catch radius comes in handy, as we saw with his toe-tapping garbage-time touchdown on Monday Night Football. He also has a goal-line fade as the lone WR on the field this season, and he's consistently targeted on breaking routes about 10 yards down the field. With Jordyn Tyson realistically targeting a Week 9 return, Vele is looking like a high-end rental.

31. Denzel Boston (at NYJ) - 49.5 proj. receiving yards

McConkey (foot) did not practice on Wednesday.

33. Malik Washington (vs. CIN) - 39.5 proj. receiving yards

34. Deebo Samuel Sr. (at SEA) - 39.5 proj. receiving yards

Update: Addison (hamstring) was back at practice on Thursday, and Justin Jefferson (ankle) plans to play.

Addison is the WR24 on WR36 usage over the past two weeks without Justin Jefferson (ankle), and it might be another outing as the alpha with the Vikings on bye in Week 6. Addison can be occasionally bullied out of his route, but there are enough downfield moments with the sprinkling of a screen to be trusted in fantasy lineups for the time being. Kyler Murray hasn't had too many anticipatory throws over the middle beyond quick seam balls, but they are using Addison on them whenever Kyler wants to deliver it. They did have a great corner route, so the rapport isn't non-existent. The bigger issue is the Vikings are 29th in neutral pass rate with a 9.1% sack rate (fifth-worst).

36. Marvin Harrison Jr. (vs. DET) - 39.5 proj. receiving yards

Marv had a productive Week 4 for the Cardinals, even if the box score was underwhelming again. He had a great ball-tracking fade TD early on, but he also drew two DPIs in and around the end zone on designed looks for him. The Cardinals also had him as the lone receiver at the goal line for a quick slant that was, of course, completely shut down. Harrison is going to be significantly better than this WR88 on WR84 usage start, and I've noticed more buy-in from him in recent weeks. If there's a week to buy low, it's against the Lions at home with a wild game total. That'd be especially true if Jeremiyah Love (ankle) is banged up.

37. KC Concepcion (at NYJ) - 39.5 proj. receiving yards

38. Keon Coleman (at LAR) - 49.5 proj. receiving yards

39. Tre Tucker (at NE) - 39.5 proj. receiving yards

40. Emeka Egbuka (at DAL) - 39.5 proj. receiving yards

Jalon Daniels was just fine in his debut as an undrafted free agent. That was the earliest into a rookie season that an UDFA QB has started a game. The Bucs tried to hide him with a season-low neutral pass rate, and Daniels is going to scramble around a bit, too. That said, Daniels has a live arm and is willing to sling it. There could be garbage-time production here. He's good enough for that.

Egbuka was only targeted three times last week, leading to a WR83 finish on WR66 usage. Playing him in fantasy is absolutely daring, as the Bucs made sure to get Chris Godwin Jr. and Cade Otton involved underneath more often. Egbuka is going to work downfield more than them, making it harder to find a floor. Egbuka hasn't been overly impressive on tape either, even if the offense is doing more creative things with him before and at the snap.

The Cowboys have the worst-graded zone defense this year, per PFF, if you're feeling risky or are just desperate. They've allowed the 10th-most fantasy points to WRs this year, most recently getting smoked by Nico Collins (WR3), Zay Flowers (104 yards on a couple dozen routes) and Stefon Diggs (WR8). The Cowboys will have new CB1 Joey Porter Jr. available for more snaps this week, and he'll very likely see Egbuka the most with Godwin hid in the slot more often. It's too much for me to bank on. The Bucs project for 19.5 points on the road.

articles.title: Cowboys-Bucs live discussion: An MVP candidate versus a rookie quarterback
articles.summary: The Cowboys take on the Bucs on Thursday night football
articles.body:
No Baker Mayfield last week for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. That meant rookie Jalon Daniels took the reins. Daniels went 9-for-27 for 148 yards, threw two interceptions, posted a 65 passer rating, and was sacked three times.

The San Francisco 49ers play the Dallas Cowboys a month from now. In my opinion, that's an NFC Championship preview.

But the Cowboys won't win a playoff game if their 32nd-ranked defense in EPA per play doesn't improve. And it's not as if teams are gashing the Cowboys, which would inflate their defensive numbers. They're dead last in success rate, too.

Something has to give on that side of the ball. There's only one way for Daniels to go. Without Joey Porter Jr., Dallas has been more than accommodating to opposing offenses. He's not in uniform tonight.

Dak Prescott has been surgical this season. Only Brock Purdy and Lamar Jackson have generated a higher EPA. Prescott has an 8-to-1 touchdown-to-interception ratio. Historically, he's been aggressive against the blitz. That does not bode well for a Todd Bowles defense. It could be a long night for a Tampa Bay secondary without Antoine Winfield.

My gut says 31-14, Cowboys. But this is not a team that wins comfortably. Their defense won't allow it. So I'll go 28-24 in an exciting Thursday showdown.

articles.title: Athlete of the Week: Blake Shaffer
articles.summary: lake Shaffer started playing football at a young age. He continued that into high school where he has showed out for the Rifle Bears.
articles.body:
RIFLE, Colo. ( KREX ) - Blake Shaffer started playing football at a young age. He continued that into high school where he has showed out for the Rifle Bears.

"It's like the chess of sports," Shaffer said. "The contact, Friday Night Lights, you can just go out and hit someone and it feels great scoring touchdowns."

He started football in third grade. Shaffer was a running back in his early days before switching and playing more receiver and tight end. A wrestler as well, Shaffer prefers football and said he made is favorite memory this year.

"It feels great getting long runs and you can hear the crowd," he said. "Coal Ridge this year, we were down two touchdowns and then I got that one touchdown to bring us to one touchdown and it just felt great hearing the crowd."

That touchdown and the win over Coal Ridge helped set the tone for the season. Shaffer had a big performance and has continued that play all year.

"You could tell it was more hype," Shaffer said about the win over Coal Ridge. "We felt good to win because from the last two years we didn't really feel it a lot. It just kept pushing us because we wanted to keep winning after that."

Shaffer made the switch to running back for Rifle coming into the season. Throw in a brand new playbook and he had plenty to work on coming into the year. He has handled it all in stride.

"Practicing running back and going into camp and everything I was like, 'Yeah, I really, I love this position,'" he said. "My senior year I really wanted to pop off and play with my brothers under the lights."

He has popped off in a big way. He has three games with over 200 yards. In his past two games he has five touchdowns and 470 total yards.

"It's been great," he said. "As a team, we're a lot closer, it's more of a brotherhood. I think because we all got the new playbook together, we all had to learn it together and I really feel like it brought us even closer because we just had to learn it together and go through our ups and downs together."

Shaffer thanked his parents, coaches and teammates for their support. He shouted his teammate Cache Garcia and his offensive line for their play.

articles.title: Bears running game looms as huge factor vs. Packers — but will Kyle Monangai play?
articles.summary: CHICAGO — When it comes to the Chicago Bears and Green Bay Packers, you can never take any statistical advantage as a given. But there’s one phase of the gam...
articles.body:
CHICAGO — When it comes to the Chicago Bears and Green Bay Packers, you can never take any statistical advantage as a given. But there's one phase of the game — at least on paper — the Bears seem to have the Packers over a barrel: the running game.

The Bears enter Sunday's Week 5 matchup at Lambeau Field boasting the No. 1 rushing offense at 196.3 yards per game. Conversely, the Packers run defense ranks 28th, allowing 139.3 yards per game.

However, Bears running backs coach Eric Studesville doesn't see a vulnerability at all.

"The (defensive) front is impressive," he said. "The backers are really impressive. I think (linebacker) Zaire Franklin's a good addition for them. (Linebacker Edgerrin) Cooper going down (with a torn Achilles) is different, but (Isaiah) McDuffie's going to be in there. He's going to play his tail off.

"The safeties (Evan Williams and Xavier McKinney) and the nickel (Javon Bullard) are really good players, and so I think this day is going to be a great challenge for us. But if we go and do what we're supposed to do, we'll have a chance."

Bears running backs Kyle Monangai and D'Andre Swift rank seventh and eighth among the league's rushing leaders with 324 and 311 yards, respectively.

Monangai ranks sixth among qualifiers with 5.4 yards per carry.

According to Next Gen Stats, Monangai reaches the line of scrimmage in just 2.50 seconds on average, the fastest mark among 39 running backs with at least 30 carries.

"He's aggressive and decisive," Studesville said. "He's a vertical cut, but he's a tough, physical runner, runs behind his pads. He brings a physicality to our offense, and that gives us juice."

On a 30-carry, 146-yard day against the New York Jets, Monangai had 106 yards after contact — the fifth-highest mark in a game this season, behind two runs apiece from the Atlanta Falcons' Bijan Robinson and Kansas City Chiefs' Kenneth Walker — and three runs of at least 10 yards.

After Swift fumbled in the third quarter, Monangai finished with 19 carries for 96 yards, including a 26-yarder, and a touchdown.

"Happy for him," Swift said Thursday. "He finished the game how he's supposed to. Had a hell of a game."

The hiccup for Week 5 is that Monangai missed a second consecutive day of practice Thursday with thumb and toe injuries. Coach Ben Johnson said earlier this week that the thumb injury shouldn't be an issue, but he hadn't addressed Monangai's toe injury.

Swift was limited in practice with hip and knee injuries. He had 15 carries for 58 yards against the Jets, but the biggest blemish of his day was the lost fumble, his second of the season.

"That ain't me," Swift said. "So I'm not about to make it a thing. Just be more conscious of it."

Another flaw for the Bears has been their lack of effectiveness in the red zone (42.11%, ranked 30th), an area of emphasis all week. But red-zone rushing probably has been particularly galling for Ben Johnson, as big a disciple of the run as there is in the league.

In the first series against the Jets, Swift saw touchdown runs from the 3- and 1-yard lines reversed on replay. The Bears turned the ball over on downs.

On the next series, the Bears drove to the Jets 4, but it took three straight tries for Monangai to cross the goal line.

"Very" frustrating, Swift said. "Because I think if we clean up the red-zone scoring we'll be in a better position offensively with points and things like that. But got to get it in there. Got to score on the first drive."

Swifts other fumble this season also came in the red zone: He fumbled near the goal line against the Minnesota Vikings in Week 2.

The Bears converted 100% of red-zone trips against the Panthers, but the fact they went 0 for 3 against the Vikings and converted 40% versus the Philadelphia Eagles and 29% against the Jets over the last three weeks has been "disappointing," offensive coordinator Press Taylor said.

"Certain teams have played us maybe a little bit differently than we planned for based on whatever they saw on us," he said. "So we're trying to make sure we do a great job self-scouting, things like that.

"But ultimately it's something we got to get cleaned up, and I think we're on the right track of doing that. But it's got to show up for us."

Guards Jonah Jackson (ankle) and Joe Thuney (pectoral) and right tackle Darnell Wright (ankle) all returned to practice Thursday after missing Wednesday's session.

Quarterback Caleb Williams (hamstring) and linebacker Keyshaun Elliott (quad) missed practice.

However, defensive backs Kyler Gordon (calf) and Cam Lewis (hip) were full participants, as were linebacker Noah Sewell (Achilles) and Shemar Turner (knee).

Gordon, Sewell and Turner remained on the reserve/physically unable to perform list as of Thursday but have been practicing in their respective 21-day return-to-pay windows.

articles.title: #1 Huskers Sweep #15 Indiana
articles.summary: The Huskers stay on top behind strong performances from Harper Murray and Teraya Sigler
articles.body:
It was an early evening top 25 showdown for the Huskers and the Hoosiers. Nebraska came out hot in the first set and carried that out into the second. Indiana kept set three much closer before the Huskers pulled away in the end.

Harper Murray led all hitters with 11 kills after having only 1 kill in the first set, she also had one ace, seven digs, and two blocks. Teraya Sigler was right behind her with 10 kills and two blocks. Mania Ogbechie had eight kills and six blocks while hitting .500. Olivia Mach had 10 kills and three service aces.

The Huskers hit a .379 on the night, allowing Indiana to hit .282, higher than what they typically allow.

Coach Dani Busboom Kelly added a new look that we hadn't seen before. She had both Mania Ogbechie and Kenna Cogill playing front row at the same time late in the match to help the Husker block. It definitely paid off.

The Huskers started off the match with a behind the setter kill from Mania Ogbechie, followed by an Andi Jackson kill. Bergan Reilly spread the offense out and the Huskers first five points came from kills from five different hitters. The Huskers got out to an early 8-2 lead. Indiana battled back a few points with an ace and tooling the block. The Huskers led going into the media time out 15-9. Bergan Reilly came out of the time out and threw down two kills. The Huskers were first to 20, however Indiana started to come alive with their block. The Huskers end the set with a big block themselves.

Nebraska hit .375 while holding Indiana to .179. Teraya Sigler led all hitters with 5 kills on the set.

Olivia Mauch served the Huskers first ace of the match putting the Huskers up 2-1. Both teams were picking up a lot off the floor for a long rally with Virginia Adriano seeing a lot of action and finally killing the ball. Laney Choboy got her 20th ace of the season to put the Huskers up 7-2. After a phantom net call on Andi Jackson that was challenged and somehow stood, the Huskers were the first to 15, leading 15-11. This was a set of challenges as both teams challenged a block touch and won their challenges. Harper Murray made some smart shots and gave the Huskers some crucial kills down the line, including a back row bomb to end the set.

The Huskers hit .400 in the second set, but allowed Indiana to hit .333.

Both teams added two blocks in this set making them tied at 4 each.

Indiana starts off the set on 2-0 run. After a few errors, the Huskers even up the score 3-3 with a solid block. The Huskers go on a 5-0 run with Harper Murray behind the service line. Teraya Sigler and Andi Jackson had some monster kills and Murray added another ace. Laney Choboy and Olivia Mauch were digging everything in that run as well. A few Husker errors and Hoosier kills even up the score at 10. An Ogbechie kill ends a 4-0 run for Indiana. Mauch gets two more aces to give the Huskers the lead again 14-13. Once again the Huskers go on a run with Harper Murray behind the service line. There was a rally that had Murray saving the ball while running all the way into the bench, and then coming back to put the point away with a back row crusher. Once again the Huskers were the first to 20. In an interesting wrinkle, DBK puts Kenna Cogill in the front row while keeping Ogbechie in too and they sealed the match with two blocks.

While the Huskers started the set off with quite a few uncharacteristic errors, the rallied and ended set three hitting .357.

The Huskers next game is a Saturday night black out against Wisconsin at Bob Devaney sports center at 6pm.

articles.summary: In August, Caitlin Clark made a quiet gesture that carried special meaning for an Indiana Fever supporter’s family.
articles.body: In August, Caitlin Clark made a quiet gesture that carried special meaning for an Indiana Fever supporter’s family. It showed that Clark had contributed $2,000 to the fundraiser, adding a personal touch to an effort created to honour Jess.The campaign is not simply designed to raise money in her memory. Its goal is to create useful resources for children in local classrooms. Funds will support Buddy Benches and provide books, giving Jess’ memory a place within the community she cared about.A supporter account, Caitlin Clark Style, shared the news on X:“Caitlin donated to Jess’s @FeverBandwagon GoFundMe 🥺✨The fundraiser will provide Buddy Benches and books for local classrooms in Jess’s memory.”The gesture also reflects the relationship Clark has built with Fever fans since entering the WNBA. articles.title: A'ja Wilson wins record fifth MVP as first three-peat in WNBA history strengthens all-time greatness case
articles.summary: The Las Vegas Aces star's fifth WNBA MVP puts her alongside Bill Russell, Kareem Abdul-Jabbar and Michael Jordan in rarefied historic air.
articles.body: On Thursday, A’ja Wilson added another line to her already lengthy basketball resume, reaching yet another level of WNBA greatness by becoming the league’s first five-time MVP. The Las Vegas Aces superstar has claimed the coveted trophy for a third consecutive season, becoming the first player in league history to win three straight MVP awards. It marks her fourth MVP title in the past five years. Aces coach Becky Hammon believes Wilson’s résumé already places her among the greatest players in basketball. In addition to her WNBA accomplishments, Wilson won an NCAA Division I national championship at South Carolina. DREAM MOVE WITHIN ONE WIN OF FIRST WNBA FINALS APPEARANCE SINCE 2013 AFTER OVERTIME VICTORY "(As) I said, take her off Mount Rushmore — she’s Everest," Hammon said earlier in the playoffs. "Now I’m taking her off Everest, and I have to put her on a different planet. She just has all of it." Hammon also emphasized that talent alone does not guarantee the kind of sustained team and individual success Wilson has achieved. "Because you can be a really talented and skilled basketball player and not win as much as she has, and not become as individually great as she has." Wilson may not have put together the most statistically impressive season of her career, but she remained dominant across the board. Her 26.2 points per game led the WNBA in scoring, while her 79 blocks were also a league high. She ranked among the league’s top five rebounders in rebounds per game during the regular season. Atlanta Dream forward Angel Reese led the WNBA with 12.1 rebounds per game and was named the 2026 WNBA Defensive Player of the Year. Other notable former WNBA players with multiple MVP awards When Wilson won her fourth MVP award in 2025, she broke a tie with Hall of Famers Sheryl Swoopes, Lisa Leslie and Lauren Jackson for the most MVP trophies in WNBA history at the time. The three standout players largely traded the award between 2000 and 2010, winning every MVP except in 2008, when Candace Parker claimed the honor, and 2009, when Diana Taurasi won. SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER In NBA history, only three players have been awarded at least five MVPs: Bill Russell, Kareem Abdul-Jabbar and Michael Jordan. With her fifth MVP, Wilson is now among select group of legendary basketball players. "If you’re able to set a standard, if you’re able to rewrite things, and kind of etch yourself into history books, it means a lot," Wilson said at a news conference in Las Vegas on Thursday. "I’m so grateful that I can share these moments with so many different people. But it’s always fun when you’re able to set the standard, and give people and yourself something to chase after." Minnesota Lynx rookie Olivia Miles finished second with six first-place votes, followed by Indiana Fever guard Kelsey Mitchell with two. Mitchell’s teammate, Caitlin Clark, received the remaining first-place vote and finished fourth. A’ja Wilson’s latest challenge is guiding the Aces through unprecedented territory. They would have to become the first team in WNBA history to erase a 2-0 deficit against the Golden State Valkyries and win a best-of-five playoff series. If Wilson leads the comeback, it would further cement her place in basketball lore. Game 3 is scheduled for Friday night as the series shifts to Las Vegas.

articles.title: EXCLUSIVE | ‘In reality, it really isn’t’: Asian Games gold medallist Pranavi Urs on golf’s ‘rich man’s sport’ image
articles.summary: \"A lot of non-golfers don't know what the sport means or what it is. And they all just think that it's a rich man's sport.
articles.body: "A lot of non-golfers don't know what the sport means or what it is. And they all just think that it's a rich man's sport. In reality, it really isn't."Pranavi Urs, the 23-year-old from Mysuru, has just returned from the Asian Games as the first Indian woman to win an individual golf gold. The medal has changed her place in Indian golf, but she is more interested in what it can do for the sport itself."I think any medal for golf at this point in the golfing world is great for India. So I think any medal, whether it's on the men's side or the women's side, would have brought a lot more attention to the sport, which obviously, at the end of the day, is the goal for us - to give back to the sport and kind of make it global and grow it in India," she told Timesofindia.com from Mysuru."Because I feel like in India, it's definitely picked up in the last few years, but it's not where it should be. And I think getting this gold home, or even the silver, I think is a good step and it's heading in the right direction."Women's golf in India: Pranavi Urs wants more attentionThat is a bigger ambition than the medal sitting in her collection. And Pranavi sees the women's game as an important part of it. "I think the girls are doing far better than the guys globally. Four or five years ago, there were only one or two girls on the LET (Ladies European Tour), with full status. Now there are five of us."So I think to just go out there and tell everyone and make a statement that the girls are good, and that we're better than the guys, and bring a lot more attention towards women's sports in India; and it doesn't have to be golf."I feel like in this Asian Games, women in sport have done a lot better than the guys. And it just shows that girls don't just sit at home.Her own career offers an example of that progress. In December 2025, Pranavi became the first Indian woman to win a professional open-field tournament against male golfers when she won the IGPL Invitational Mumbai. She shot a bogey-free 8-under 60 in the final round and won by two strokes.Pranavi's Asian Games campaign also brought a team silver, with Aditi and Diksha Dagar joining her on the podium in the women's event. Aditi had won individual silver at Hangzhou in 2023, becoming the first Indian golfer to win an Asian Games medal. She was also the first Indian to win on the Ladies European Tour, has five LET titles, has played at three Olympics and finished fourth at Tokyo, one shot off the medals.Aditi Ashok's influence and the support behind Pranavi UrsFor Pranavi, Aditi has been a reference point since she was a junior. "Aditi is on a different level. She's my senior. I've looked up to her since I was a little kid, since I was a junior. We have quite similar careers, apart from the fact that I haven't won on the LET yet. She's still the greatest golfer in India."Pranavi's own career began much earlier, at a golf course in Mysuru when she was six. The route since then has taken her through junior golf, the professional ranks and the LET with support around her through all of it."I think I wouldn't have done it without my family. My family has been my biggest support. I've got a really good support system. I have my coach, my S&C coach, my psychologist, my physio. So I've got a really strong base, and I can lean on them whenever I need to. We've got a really good bond. Everyone gets along really well. So I think I've achieved what I've achieved because of my family and my support system."That support is what she points to when asked about the next generation, rather than rankings or prize money. "I just want young girls to pick up a sport, love it, enjoy it, and have fun with it."I didn't grow up playing golf because I wanted fame or money. I play golf because I love the sport. And money and fame is just a bonus.The money has, nevertheless, become hard to miss after the 2026 Games. Karnataka Govt. announced ₹1 crore for her individual gold and ₹75 lakh for the team silver. The IGPL announced another ₹1 crore for the individual gold, while the Indian Golf Union also announced a reward.For a young golfer looking at what is possible in the sport, Pranavi believes the rewards can be an incentive too. "For someone who thinks like make money or X, Y and Z ... if that motivates them, then sure, so be it. I’m very happy that it's all out there in public for people to see what they can get if they achieve something. So let them be motivated by that. I think each to their own, right? I feel like everybody has a different goal and why they play the sport."The triple bogey that tested Pranavi Urs in NagoyaFor all the attention that came after the gold, the medal itself was in serious doubt on the third hole of the final round. Pranavi had started the day with a three-shot lead. A triple bogey on the third wiped it out."I think I lost my lead, which was unfortunate, not because of a bad shot, but I just got unlucky on the third. It was out of my control where the ball ended up and what happened."She was one shot behind by the fourth, but her response was not to start chasing every lost shot. "I was like, 'You know what, it's fine. You've hit rock bottom.’ I was one back on the fourth hole. And I was like, ‘You always love chasing. You've already hit rock bottom. Just play fearless and you can do it.'"There was - she remembered - another golfer, a certain Rory McIlroy, who had been in a similar position.I did think about Rory because he had a bad start at the Masters when he won it for the first time. And I was like, ‘If he can do it, so can you.’ So, you know, just keep at it. Just stick to your process.The process, she kept coming back to, was simple: stay patient. "There was not a single moment when I didn't think I was not going to win. You just keep doing what you have to do, stick to your process, and just be patient, because it's 18 holes. If I didn't win on the third hole after what happened, that's fine. It's 18 holes."She eventually finished with a 70 for a 15-under 265, one shot clear of China's Yin Ruoning, a former world No. 1 and winner of the 2023 Women's PGA Championship, and Singapore's Shannon Tan, who plays on the Ladies European Tour."All I wanted to do was obviously hole the [final] putt. I don't remember most of it. I was just in the flow. I remember every shot, but I don't remember it as much as I remember the last part, because obviously there are videos and stuff now."And the ability to stay in that flow was something Pranavi learned by spending the last three years playing on the LET, moving between countries, courses and conditions. The travel itself has become part of the job."I think I'm more experienced now because I play in Europe. It's different conditions week in, week out. You've got jet lag, you've got different places, different rooms. You've just got to go with the flow. Just going with the flow and adapting to whatever comes your way - whether it's nervousness or anything - just being able to deal with it and move on."From Asian Games gold to the search for an LET titleAt the 2023 Asian Games, Pranavi finished 13th individually, and the Indian women's team finished fourth. And that is where much of the difference between Hangzhou and Nagoya lies for her. "It's a mental sport. You've got to stay focused, you've got to stay patient.""And, like I said, just kind of preparing yourself week in, week out and travelling around the world, fighting jet lag, fighting being homesick and all of that has helped me grow into a better person and a better golfer." she added.Now, the one thing still missing from her professional record is an LET title. She has had several high finishes in Europe, but no victory yet. “Every golfer has their doubts. If you're not winning, you're like, 'Will I ever win?'", said Pranavi, but Aichi-Nagoya has given her belief that she will eventually win."I beat a world No. 6, so if I can do that, I can win on the LET. Just be patient, keep doing what I'm doing, and eventually I will win. Every golfer goes to win. You give 100%, 200%. That's why golfers go to win. Eventually, I will win."And then there is one small matter of one more first that she wants."An Olympic gold."Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.body: El luchador mexicano Hijo de Fishman fue detenido tras lanzar al árbitro Gerardo Germán Pineda contra el ring para posteriormente aplicarle un 'piledriver' (también conocido como martinete o desnucadora), una llave prohibida por su alta peligrosidad. 'Telemundo' informó que el árbitro de 75 años, que en su época de luchador era conocido como El Búho, murió sobre el cuadrilátero. Una testigo presencial asegura que Hijo de Fishman y el árbitro discutieron antes del incidente mortal, que se produjo en el Centro Deportivo Cultural 11 de Julio, en Mineral de la Reforma (México) durante la disputa de una velada llamada 'Deslealtades'. El Hijo de Fishman, que es luchador de segunda generación (es hijo de José Ángel Nájera Sánchez), participaba en la lucha estelar contra Máscara Sagrada NG. Policías municipales lo detuvieron y lo entregaron a la Procuraduría General de Justicia del Estado de Hidalgo, que podría acusar al luchador de homicidio culposo.

articles.title: Guardians force decisive ALDS Game 5 as White Sox miss chance to reach first ALCS since 2005
articles.summary: White Sox-Guardians ALDS Game 4 saw Cleveland erupt for two fifth-inning home runs to erase Chicago's lead and force a decisive Game 5 Saturday.
articles.body: With three of the four spots in the league championship series already clinched, Thursday night’s White Sox-Guardians matchup was the lone game on MLB’s postseason schedule. It gave Chicago an opportunity to end its long American League Championship Series drought. Instead, the White Sox came up short, falling 9-5 in Game 4. articles.title: Pere Navarro sentencia al no lograr rebajar la tasa de alcohol al volante: "el interés general no está de moda"
articles.standfirst: El máximo responsable de Tráfico se ha lamentado en un acto con 'Cerveceros de España' de que haya quedado en suspenso la ley que pretendía rebajar los límites máximos de alcohol
articles.summary: El máximo responsable de Tráfico se ha lamentado en un acto con 'Cerveceros de España' de que haya quedado en suspenso la ley que pretendía rebajar los límites máximos de alcohol
articles.body: Pere Navarro ha acompañado a Jacobo Olaya, presidente de Cerveceros de España, en la presentación de la campaña 'Elegir SIN al volante es la caña', que se ha dado a conocer junto a los resultados del estudio 'Hábitos y contextos de consumo de la cerveza SIN'. Entre las conclusiones de este, recogidas por Europa Press, se han desvelado datos tan concluyentes como que el 47,3% de los conductores eligen la cerveza sin alcohol como bebida cuando tienen que conducir. Pero la ocasión ha sido propicia para preguntar al máximo responsable de Tráfico por la ley que pretendía rebajar la tasa de alcohol permitida al volante. El tema ya estaba en marcha y el 29 de septiembre fue aprobada en el Pleno el Congreso la toma en consideración de la proposición de ley para modificar el artículo 76 de la ley de Tráfico. Lo que proponía esta modificación, entre otras cosas, es que 0,1 mg/litro de aire o 0,2 g/litro en sangre fueran ya consideradas como infracción grave. Es decir, que una caña o media copa de vino se convirtieran ya en una infracción en caso de ser pillado el conductor en un control de alcoholemia. Pero todo esto se ha venido abajo una vez que Pedro Sánchez ha disuelto las Cortes y convocado elecciones. "El tema estaba atado, parecía que iba a salir, pero se han convocado elecciones", ha dicho Navarro, que reconocía que "el lobby del alcohol, en su derecho, fue a ver a todos los grupos parlamentarios", y que estos han tenido que elegir entre "el lobby del alcohol" o las víctimas de tráfico. En su costumbre de exponer su punto de vista con claridad, Navarro ha ido más lejos al decir que "es una decisión ética y moral y cada uno que asuma su responsabilidad. Yo creo que el trabajo está hecho y es un cuestión solo de tiempo el que al final podamos verlo aprobado. Tiempo al tiempo". Ante este bloqueo al gran proyecto de actualizar la actual tasa de alcoholemia, que lleva ya 28 años en vigor, el Director General de Tráfico ha lamentado que "el interés general no está de moda".

articles.title: El caso Carvajal desata la crítica de Pepe Brasín: “Tiene que haber excepciones”
articles.standfirst: El periodista cuestiona en 'La Tribu' la rigidez del fair play financiero de LaLiga y también se pronuncia sobre los posibles pitos a Mbappé en el Bernabéu
articles.summary: El periodista cuestiona en 'La Tribu' la rigidez del fair play financiero de LaLiga y también se pronuncia sobre los posibles pitos a Mbappé en el Bernabéu
articles.body: El posible fichaje de Dani Carvajal por el Getafe ha reabierto el debate sobre las restricciones económicas de LaLiga. Pepe Brasín, en su intervención en 'La Tribu', ha cuestionado la rigidez del fair play financiero, una herramienta que considera fundamental para la estabilidad de los clubes, pero que, en su opinión, necesita una revisión para evitar situaciones como la del futbolista español. “El fair play financiero ha sido, en mi opinión, muy muy bueno para la liga”, ha comenzado explicando Brasín, recordando que anteriormente existía “un descontrol económico que llevaba a riesgo de desaparición a no pocos equipos”. Sin embargo, considera que las restricciones actuales están limitando el crecimiento de la competición y la capacidad de los clubes para ilusionar a sus aficionados. Para Brasín, la situación del posible fichaje de Carvajal por el Getafe es un ejemplo de hasta dónde pueden llegar las restricciones económicas. “Creo que el Fair Play Financiero debería ser un pelín menos estricto en ciertas cosas, y aquí entra el asunto Carvajal”, ha asegurado. El periodista ha cuestionado que LaLiga pueda impedir una operación pese a que exista un acuerdo económico entre el jugador y el club: “¿Cómo puede ser que a un jugador con el que se llega a un acuerdo por X dinero, directamente LaLiga diga 'no, este jugador vale más dinero y tú no lo puedes fichar'?”. Aunque entiende que esta normativa nació para evitar posibles fraudes, considera que ha llegado el momento de flexibilizar algunos aspectos. “Tiene que haber excepciones, no sólo tiene que haber excepciones, sino que tiene que haber cierta relajación en algunos puntos concretos del Fair Play Financiero”, ha defendido. Además, Brasín ha advertido de las consecuencias de mantener unas restricciones tan exigentes: “Que seamos tan absolutamente cerrados en algunos temas creo que lleva a una parálisis económica y a una parálisis a la hora de generar ilusión”. En este sentido, ha definido el caso Carvajal como “la punta del iceberg” y ha planteado la necesidad de que los clubes profesionales revisen determinadas normas. “LaLiga ha llegado hasta aquí con unas normas que eran necesarias. Bueno, va siendo hora de que las retoquemos un poco”, ha concluido sobre este asunto. Pepe Brasín también se ha pronunciado sobre la situación de Kylian Mbappé y la posibilidad de que el público del Santiago Bernabéu reciba al delantero francés con silbidos en el partido frente al Villarreal. “El público del Bernabéu tiene suficientes argumentos para atronadoras pitadas diarias y constantes a su equipo". Sobre Mbappé, Brasín ha apuntado a “su cierta displicencia, con sus apariciones o desapariciones en público y en privado, también con su manera de jugar”, aunque reconoce su capacidad goleadora. Sin embargo, cree que los aficionados deberían esperar al desarrollo del encuentro antes de mostrar su descontento. “Cosa diferente es que se ponga el Villarreal 0-1. Cosa diferente es que el partido no vaya por los cauces de juego adecuados. Y ahí sí, ahí se desatarán los pitos”, ha advertido Brasín, que no considera necesario que el Bernabéu comience el partido con un ambiente hostil.

Mbappé, en un entrenamiento. Realmadrid.com

articles.title: Roberto Gómez responde a los rumores sobre Sergio Ramos y el Getafe
articles.standfirst: El periodista de Radio MARCA aclara lo que sabe sobre el posible interés del conjunto azulón en el central y señala el deseo de Ángel Torres de contar con Dani Carvajal
articles.summary: El periodista de Radio MARCA aclara lo que sabe sobre el posible interés del conjunto azulón en el central y señala el deseo de Ángel Torres de contar con Dani Carvajal
articles.body: Roberto Gómez ha protagonizado una nueva intervención en La Tribu, en la que ha abordado algunos de los asuntos de la actualidad futbolística. Uno de los protagonistas ha sido el Getafe, especialmente por los nombres que podrían estar relacionados con el futuro del conjunto azulón. El periodista ha respondido a los rumores sobre Sergio Ramos, ha hablado de Dani Carvajal y ha aprovechado para elogiar la gestión de Ángel Torres. Durante la conversación, Roberto Gómez ha sido preguntado directamente por el supuesto interés del Getafe en Sergio Ramos. Su respuesta ha sido clara: "No, a mí no me consta". El periodista también ha sido cuestionado por la información que había adelantado el día anterior sobre un posible bombazo. Sin embargo, ha querido dejar claro que no había señalado al central como protagonista de esa operación: "Sí, pero yo no he dicho que sea Sergio Ramos". Ante la insistencia sobre si el nombre del futbolista estaba bien encaminado, Roberto Gómez ha vuelto a mostrarse contundente: "Es que ni idea, ni idea". Eso sí, el periodista ha puesto sobre la mesa otro nombre relacionado con el conjunto azulón: Dani Carvajal. "Lo único que sé es que al Getafe, sobre todo al presidente, le gustaría contar con Dani Carvajal, pero hay una situación que yo creo que es bastante complicada", ha explicado. Más allá de los posibles movimientos del Getafe, Roberto Gómez ha querido destacar el trabajo de Ángel Torres al frente de la entidad madrileña. "Me parece, sinceramente, el mejor presidente que hay en el fútbol español", ha asegurado. El periodista ha insistido en el mérito que tiene mantener al equipo durante tantos años en la máxima categoría: "El presidente que más mérito tiene en la primera división del fútbol español se llama Ángel Torres. Es impresionante lo que ha conseguido mantenerse y jugar Europa". Además, ha reivindicado el trabajo de clubes como el Getafe y el Rayo Vallecano, que, a su juicio, deben superar numerosas dificultades: "¿Qué mérito tiene el Getafe? Mucho. ¿Qué mérito tiene el Rayo Vallecano? ¿Qué mérito tienen estos equipos que además tienen muchos impedimentos de otros organismos?". La intervención también ha dejado espacio para hablar del regreso de LaLiga y del posible recibimiento a Mbappé por parte de la afición madridista. Roberto Gómez ha mostrado su desacuerdo con centrar el debate en los pitos al francés. "Que la gente acude a los campos con ilusión, con felicidad, con ganas sobre todo de apoyar a su equipo", ha concluido.

articles.title: Coki Nieto tampoco jugará en Milán y Yanguas tiene nuevo compañero provisional
articles.standfirst: El madrileño ha anunciado que, tras perderse Dusseldorf, tampoco estará en la cita italiana de la próxima semana debido a unas molestias
articles.summary: El madrileño ha anunciado que, tras perderse Dusseldorf, tampoco estará en la cita italiana de la próxima semana debido a unas molestias
articles.body: El madrileño Coki Nieto tampoco estará en el Milan P1 de Premier Padel que se disputará del 12 al 20 de octubre. El revés anunció hace unos días unas molestias físicas que le impedirían estar en el torneo de Dusseldorf de esta semana, y anoche confirmó que tampoco estará en la prueba italiana. "He decidido recuperar y poder llegar bien en el resto de temporada", explicaba en sus redes sociales hace unas horas. Una ausencia que se produce a menos de un mes del inicio del Mundial, donde ha sido uno de los elegidos por Juanjo Gutiérrez. Sería su tercera cita mundialista con la absoluta de España. Ante esto, su compañero en Premier Padel, Mike Yanguas, ha decidido escoger a otro jugador disputar con él la prueba de Milán. Se trata del gallego Pablo Lijó, 46 del ránking FIP, y con el que saldrá como pareja 8 en el torneo. Después llegará una semana de parón y, tras ella, la gira asiática con el Major de Kuwait como primera prueba antes de la cita mundialista de Qatar la semana siguiente. La prudencia médica con Coki pasa por estar en ambos torneos, claves para la temporada 2026, y se espera que con estas tres semanas de descanso llegue en plenas condiciones.

articles.title: Ryan Hall: Leeds Rhinos winger announces retirement at 38
articles.summary: Leeds Rhinos legend Ryan Hall announces his retirement at the age of 38.
articles.body:
Leeds Rhinos legend Ryan Hall has announced his retirement at the age of 38.

The winger made his senior debut for the Rhinos in May 2007 and went on to score 358 tries in 540 career appearances.

The former England international, who also had spells with Sydney Roosters and Hull KR, won six Grand Finals and two Challenge Cups with Leeds.

"I think the time's right that I hang up the boots. I've done it for 20 years and I've loved every minute of it," he told the club website. , external

"The club's in a good position to go with the youth, that's the natural progression in rugby league."

Hall, who will move into a commercial role at the club, is Super League's second highest scorer with 274, seven behind Leigh winger Josh Charnley.

He left Leeds for Sydney Roosters after the 2018 season but failed to score a try in 11 NRL appearances across two seasons.

Hull KR brought him back to Super League for the 2021 campaign and he scored 62 tries in 102 games for the Robins before returning to Leeds two years ago.

He scored 10 times in 24 appearances in 2026 as the Rhinos finished second and his final appearance for the club came in their play-off semi-final defeat by Warrington at Headingley.

"I am pleased to have had the honour to work with Ryan over the last couple of years," head coach Brad Arthur said.

"He has performed at the very highest level for his club and country and he leaves the field on his terms, having maintained his presence for 20 years; that is a remarkable achievement."

The club have said Hall, who scored 39 tries in 40 appearances for England and was part of the side that finished runner-up in the 2017 World Cup final, will make a "cameo appearance" in a pre-season match against Hull FC in January as part of a testimonial.

articles.summary: El evento tendrá lugar en el Centro Deportivo Municipal Gallur y se disputará bajo el formato H6
articles.body: Madrid se prepara para acoger la primera edición del HYATLÓN ÁMBAR TOUR, una competición que pondrá a prueba los límites de los deportistas los próximos días 10 y 11 de octubre de 2026. El evento tendrá lugar en el Centro Deportivo Municipal Gallur, convirtiéndose en el centro de fitness racing durante el fin de semana. La prueba de Madrid se disputará bajo el formato H6. Este formato consiste en intercalar seis kilómetros de carrera con seis estaciones de ejercicios funcionales. Dado que la competición es en pista cubierta, cada segmento de 1.000 metros de carrera equivale a completar cinco vueltas a la pista de 200 metros de Gallur. El mapa del evento está diseñado para optimizar el flujo de la competición. La pista de atletismo rodeará la zona interior, la cual es un área de acceso controlado donde se ubican las estaciones, la zona de calentamiento, la cámara de llamadas y las zonas de relevo. Cada estación cuenta con zonas de entrada (IN) y salida (OUT) debidamente señalizadas que los deportistas deberán respetar de manera estricta. Bloque 1: 1.000 m de carrera (5 vueltas) seguidos de la estación de SkiErg (1.000 m). Bloque 2: 1.000 m de carrera (5 vueltas) seguidos de la estación de Sled Push (50 m). Bloque 3: 1.000 m de carrera (5 vueltas) seguidos de la estación de Burpee Broad Jump (80 m completados en 2 vueltas). Bloque 4: 1.000 m de carrera (5 vueltas) seguidos de la estación de RowErg (1.000 m). Bloque 5: 1.000 m de carrera (5 vueltas) seguidos de la estación de Sandbag Lunges (100 m). Bloque 6: 1.000 m de carrera (5 vueltas) seguidos de la estación de Wall Balls (100 repeticiones). Final: Tramo señalizado hasta cruzar la meta.
