articles.title: New York Knicks star reveals the exact players who do not love the second apron
articles.summary: A veteran New York Knicks player has shared his thoughts on the second apron, as the team try to navigate the difficulties of bringing back Karl-Anthony Town...
articles.body:
A veteran New York Knicks player has shared his thoughts on the second apron, as the team try to navigate the difficulties of bringing back Karl-Anthony Towns.

The reigning champions are one of the two teams in the first apron, but are only $3.2 million dollars below the second apron, and are still without a confirmation on a deal for KAT.

Moreover, they also have players like Jalen Brunson, OG Anunoby and Josh Hart, who are also extension-eligible. This makes the situation extremely challenging for Team President Leon Rose, as the team will struggle to keep the core that helped win a championship unless players are willing to take a significant pay cut.

Jalen Brunson led the way in doing that when he signed the four-year, $156 million deal, as a result of which he gave up $113 million to help build a championship roster. After winning a championship, it is not certain if players would once again take the pay cut, which could make it difficult for the Knicks.

Bruce Brown believes players do not get full mid-level because of new CBA

Due to the current CBA rules, the Knicks are not allowed to sign players using the (non-taxpayer) mid-level exception.

However, because the Knicks are champions and attracting players to play winning basketball is easier, sometimes veterans decide to move teams for stability and end up signing on lesser deals to help the team.

Bruce Brown pointed this out, and how the new CBA was making it a common theme.

"I'm sure there is. The new CBA is good for max guys, new free agents and rookie extension guys. The middle guys, it kind of sucks for us. There's not a lot of people getting that full mid-level or the tax mid-level, so it's tough," Bowen said after the Knicks preseason loss to the Washington Wizards.

Mitchell Robinson, who won the championship with the Knicks, signed a mid-level exception with the Boston Celtics. The team could not bring back the center, as they did not have the cap space to offer him a new deal.

Looking at the cap situation, they could end up losing a few more role players, which would definitely hamper their chances of competing in the Eastern Conference, where teams like the Philadelphia 76ers and the Miami Heat have made some major moves.

articles.title: Bengals' Jordan Battle: Malik Willis taps the ball before he throws, we can key on that
articles.summary: NFL players and coaches spend many hours studying film of their upcoming opponents to find tendencies that can give them an advantage on Sunday.
articles.body:
NFL players and coaches spend many hours studying film of their upcoming opponents to find tendencies that can give them an advantage on Sunday. Bengals safety Jordan Battle found such a tendency with Sunday's opponent, Dolphins quarterback Malik Willis.

For some reason, Battle decided to tell the press about it before the game, giving Willis and the Dolphins an opportunity to fix it before Sunday.

Battle told reporters in the Bengals' locker room that Willis has a tell that lets the defense know when he's about to throw the ball, so Battle and his fellow defensive backs can break on the ball a split-second earlier. Or at least they can if Willis doesn't fix it, now that Battle blabbed.

"He has a little slight little tap before every throw though, so I feel like we could use that as a key to break on the ball," Battle said. "He likes to tap the ball before he throws it, or he takes his hand off, and that that gives the read the break. He's obviously dangerous with his feet. We know we've got to be alert for that. Third and longs, they will run quarterback draws, and in the passing game, he will extend plays. So we've got to be good downfield. DBs are plastering, so we got to be alert for that. He will take chances. We just got to be on, be alert on guys where they line up."

Battle and the Bengals made a good observation in their film study. Battle's coaches and teammates may be asking him why on earth he thought it was a good idea to broadcast that observation to the public before the game.

articles.title: Eugenio Chacarra considers withdrawing despite leading the Spanish Open, ‘it’s not good’
articles.summary: Eugenio Chacarra is making a strong case to Luke Donald that he should play a key role at next year’s Ryder Cup. The Spaniard is enjoying an incredible seaso...
articles.body:
Eugenio Chacarra is making a strong case to Luke Donald that he should play a key role at next year's Ryder Cup.

The Spaniard is enjoying an incredible season on the DP World Tour, and is in the mix with Patrick Reed and Rory McIlroy for the Race to Dubai title. The 26-year-old has won twice on the DP World Tour this year and looked set for a third win at his home open.

Chacarra leads the Spanish Open after 18 holes, shooting a 66 in the opening round. This was a statement round in a field featuring Sergio Garcia, Justin Rose, and several other European Ryder Cup greats.

But it seems his tournament could be cut short, as he considers withdrawing from the lead.

Eugenio Chacarra considering withdrawing from Spanish Open with injury

Chacarra entered the week with an injury, having broken his toe while getting a glass of water in the middle of the night last week, but he didn't want to miss his national open, so he's teeing off in Spain.

This injury didn't look to have affected his performance through 18 holes, but despite shooting the best round of the day to open his tournament, Chacarra said he's suffering so much that he's considering withdrawing from the lead.

He said to the DP World Tour, "It's not good, suffering a lot. It's been tough; not sure what is going to happen tomorrow. I need to take care of myself. Obviously, I got a good round, but how I feel physically is not great.

"It doesn't hurt when I'm swinging, so I can still make a score, but it's been really tough to walk.

"The pain I had on the last 12 holes, I don't know if it is worth it as I have a lot to play the next couple of weeks.

"I've got 24 hours to rest and see how it feels in the morning. I've got a lot to play for, I've got four weeks that are really important to me."

It would be a massive disappointment for Chacarra, of course, having to withdraw from the lead of his own national open, but this would also be a blow to the tournament.

Spain's superstar Jon Rahm already withdrew before the event as he expects the birth of his fourth child, and now the country's other hope of a home winner could also be ending his week early.

Hopefully he can grind his way through the pain this week, as it would be a huge shame to see Chacarra forced out of this event when he's playing so incredibly well.

articles.title: Indiana Fever fans react to Caitlin Clark’s honest thoughts on signing ‘EPIC’ $1.3 million extension
articles.summary: Caitlin Clark was recently quizzed on being eligible for the Exceptional Performance on Initial Contract (EPIC) extension. Clark has taken the WNBA by storm...
articles.body:
Caitlin Clark was recently quizzed on being eligible for the Exceptional Performance on Initial Contract (EPIC) extension.

Clark has taken the WNBA by storm since being drafted by the Indiana Fever in 2024, setting points and assist records throughout her time with the team.

She ended the most recent season with the most total points created of any player per game and in turn, Fever fans would no doubt love for her to sign the EPIC extension.

When asked about that happening this week, though, Clark did not fully commit to saying she would sign it, but did add that she wants to 'do what's best for the team'.

What fans are saying about Caitlin Clark's 'EPIC' contract comments

Clark said: "I'm not saying I am going to sign it, not saying I'm gonna sign it or not sign it. I think it's just kind of figuring out the way we need to construct our roster.

"I mean, no matter what, I'm going to be here, I just want to do what's best for the team."

Now, fans have been reacting to the clip of Clark talking about the EPIC and the replies have been mixed.

One fan stated: "The Tom Brady approach. Take less, bring more talent, win rings. Probably smart in the long run."

Another suggested: "Your squad has finished 6th three years in a row. Fever doesn't seem to have a clear direction of who they are building around. It is foolish of her not to sign the EPIC extension."

A third wrote: "The way she's already planning around the team not herself tells you everything about who actually cares about winning."

"Caitlin Clark is making herself smaller for the Fever when it should be the Fever moulding itself around her. A true hunger to win also means refusing to play below your potential," commented a fourth.

Another tweeted: "This level of loyalty is admirable when the other side deserves it. I don't think so in this case."

A sixth added: "Caitlin will not take the EPIC to help sign Kelsey and encourage other players to the Fever. She will also have more influence on team selections. Watch this space!"

It remains to be seen what the future holds for the Fever's star players like Clark and as one fan pointed out, Kelsey Mitchell.

But should Caitlin agree to the extension, as per ESPN , she could sign for the 'projected max of $1.3 million in 2027 and the projected supermax of $1.7 million in 2028'

articles.title: Lucas Chevalier could leave PSG in January
articles.summary: Lucas Chevalier (24) could leave Paris Saint-Germain during the January transfer window, as per a report from L’Équipe. The Frenchman has failed to establish...
articles.body:
Lucas Chevalier (24) could leave Paris Saint-Germain during the January transfer window, as per a report from L'Équipe . The Frenchman has failed to establish himself at the Parc des Princes since making the move from formative club Lille OSC.

Chevalier joined PSG in the summer of 2025 for a €40m fee. He was earmarked as the replacement for Gianluigi Donnarumma, who had left to join Manchester City. However, an unconvincing first few months at his new club saw him demoted in favour of Russian goalkeeper Matvey Safonov midway through last season. Chevalier has not managed to win his place back, with Luis Enrique persisting with Safonov.

The European champions' failed attempts to recruit Zion Suzuki in the summer also show a lack of faith in the French goalkeeper, who has dropped off the radar in recent months. Should his situation fail to change by January, Chevalier would consider an exit from PSG, whilst the club would also be open to listening to offers for the goalkeeper.

articles.title: No slowing down: Skater off to world games aged 60
articles.summary: Darren Miles, who has skateboarded all his life, says the sport "matches his personality".
articles.body:
An amateur skateboarder is set to represent his country for the first time almost 50 years after he took up the sport.

Darren Miles, 60, from Plymouth, is to represent Great Britain in the slalom event at the World Skate Games in Paraguay later this month.

Miles will take part in three disciplines as part of the team made up of a mixture of professionals and amateurs.

"When I was 10 I never thought I would be skateboarding at 60 for my country so that's the main attraction," he said.

Miles first became interested in the sport in 1977 in Essex where he "always had a skateboard and always skated around".

In 2020 he "realised he was slowly losing his tricks" and took to slalom, which involves speed skateboarding around cones.

When he heads to the World Skate Games, Miles said he could be up against competitors who are in their 20s as well as those his own age.

He said "to finish and not get disqualified" would be a successful games for him.

"There's a top 16, I don't really anticipate getting into there, but I'll be going there and supporting all the other guys that are racing, because a few of the English guys are in with a good chance," he said.

"I'll be supporting them and just enjoying being at the event."

He said he enjoyed travelling for skateboarding events and the social aspect of the sport was a "big draw" for him.

"Sometimes you get a sport that's what matches your personality and it can be a lot of fun with a shared danger," he said.

"Everybody's been really supportive and I think a little bit amazed."

articles.title: Kompany backs Musiala to come back strong from latest setback
articles.summary: Jamal Musiala is Bayern Munich’s only absentee ahead of Saturday’s Bundesliga clash with FC Augsburg, head coach Vincent Kompany confirmed on Friday.The 23-y...
articles.body:
Jamal Musiala is Bayern Munich's only absentee ahead of Saturday's Bundesliga clash with FC Augsburg, head coach Vincent Kompany confirmed on Friday.

The 23-year-old has endured a frustrating run of injury setbacks in recent years and began the current season on the sidelines after suffering two collapses linked to absence seizures during pre-season.

Having worked his way back to fitness and returned to action, Musiala suffered another setback during the international break, as he was forced to leave the Germany national team camp with a thigh injury.

The German international must once again focus on his recovery, with Kompany confident he will bounce back.

"I can relate to his story of setbacks. I've experienced that often in my own career. Coming back from that is a great strength," said the former Manchester City defender at a press conference on Friday.

"I hope he can enjoy playing football again in the coming years, and I believe he will. Once you learn how to come back from moments like these, you carry that ability with you for the rest of your life," added Kompany.

"That's something Jamal has always shown. In every situation, he knows how to fight his way back, and he always comes back. We've seen how happy the team and fans are when he scores a goal. We'll experience those moments again.

"We'll do everything we can to make sure he stays fit and can perform at his best. But because he's already managed to come back before, he'll be able to do it again and again. Without a doubt."

It remains unclear when Musiala will return, but the German international took a step forward earlier this week by resuming individual training.

articles.title: Pick of the stats: Southampton v Portsmouth
articles.summary: BBC Sport highlights some of the key stats and facts for the Championship match between Southampton and Portsmouth.
articles.body:
Fresh from boss Tonda Eckert being given the all-clear to continue as Southampton boss after the Spygate affair, Saints are hoping to maintain their 100% home record in the Championship with a fifth successive victory.

South coast rivals Portsmouth make the short journey along the M27 on Sunday (12:00 BST) on a three-game unbeaten run.

The last four league encounters between Southampton and Portsmouth have all been drawn, with Pompey the last team to win in this fixture in a 4-1 victory at Fratton Park in April 2005.

Portsmouth have won one of their past nine league visits to Southampton (D4 L4), winning 2-0 in the top-flight in January 1988 under Alan Ball.

Southampton have scored 15 goals in just four home league games this season – it is the most by a Championship side in their first four home games since Reading scored 16 in 2008-09.

This is only Portsmouth's third league game on a Sunday in the past two seasons, with the previous two both against Southampton (D2). Pompey have won just four of their past 32 league games on Sundays (D11 L17).

Southampton's Cyle Larin has scored 11 goals in 14 Championship appearances at St Mary's, scoring a goal every 81 minutes. Since 2004-05, the only player to play 750+ minutes at one stadium and have a better minutes per goal ratio is Dwight Gayle at St James' Park (one every 72 mins).

articles.title: Lions Predicted to Land ‘Physical’ Eagles CB Before Trade Deadline
articles.summary: The Detroit Lions are named as a top landing spot for Philadelphia Eagles cornerback Kelee Ringo on the trade market. The post Lions Predicted to Land ‘Physi...
articles.body:
The Detroit Lions have some help on the way for their ailing secondary, but may need to hit the trade market for more reinforcement.

The Lions have struggled on defense through the start of this season, allowing opposing quarterbacks to pick apart their injured and underperforming secondary. CBS Sports analyst Jordan Dajani believes the Lions will be able to find some of that help on the trade block, connecting them to a Philadelphia Eagles defensive back who might need a change of scenery.

Lions Could Find Secondary Help on the Trade Market

Dajani broke down some of the most likely trade targets ahead of the deadline, suggesting the Lions could make a run for Eagles cornerback Kelee Ringo. Dajani noted that the Eagles could soon be losing Ringo for nothing, so they may put him on the trade block and seek any kind of modest return.

"Kelee Ringo needs a change of scenery and is in the final year of his rookie deal," Dajani wrote. "The former fourth-round pick out of Georgia has the physical makeup you want at 6-foot-2, 207 pounds. He's started in just eight of 55 career games played with the Eagles, and he has played only on special teams this season. However, there are multiple teams out there that need cornerbacks right now to come in and contribute immediately."

The Lions were in the hunt to land Joey Porter Jr. before the Dallas Cowboys closed the deal with the Pittsburgh Steelers . If they return to the trade market for more help, Ringo could be an affordable addition.

Lions Getting Another Key Return in the Secondary

The Lions already have some help on the way. They began the season with both starting safeties — Brian Branch and Kerby Joseph — on the reserve/PUP list, but could be close to getting one of them back.

Lions defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard told reporters this week that Branch is looking great and appears ready to take the field for the team's next game.

"If we were playing tonight, it would be realistic," Sheppard told reporters on Thursday. "Like, this dude—it's like he hadn't been out. I'm serious. It literally looks like he hadn't been out. It's unbelievable. So, it's just a matter of I'm going to lean on (Director of Player Health) Brett Fisher, (Head Trainer) Mike Sundeen, and our medical staff here. They've always done a tremendous job, and whatever they tell me. If that's 20 plays, if that's 30, if it's 50—I want it to be 60—but whatever they tell me, I'm going to lock that, and we're going to roll."

articles.title: Peterson’s hat trick lifts UTSA past South Florida 31-24 in Thursday night thriller
articles.summary: A’Marion Peterson seals another UTSA Alamodome victory with his third rushing touchdown of the night.
articles.body:
The UTSA Roadrunners win in the Alamodome. It's just a fact of life.

Head coach Jeff Traylor entered Thursday night's marquee matchup in the American Conference with a 25-1 record against conference opponents in the Alamodome. But his Roadrunners found themselves in unfamiliar territory against South Florida: trailing in the fourth quarter in their beloved building.

UTSA hadn't staged a fourth quarter comeback at home since 2022, but the resilient Roadrunners never panicked. They marched 75 yards down the field in 10 plays spanning 101 seconds. When it came time to deliver the finishing blow from the 1-yard line, UTSA knew exactly who to call.

Running back A'Marion Peterson previously scored twice on direct snaps Thursday night — first on a 53-yard burst, then on a 3-yard plunge. With 15 seconds remaining, Peterson punched in his third touchdown to complete the hat trick and cap a stellar 92-yard performance, his most productive career outing against an FBS opponent.

"That's a short yardage play we been working on all year," UTSA quarterback Owen McCown said of Peterson's three direct snap touchdowns. "AP is a big back, one of the three really elite backs that we have, so any time he's in we trust him 100 percent to get that one or two yards. And in that scenario with all the guys hunched down with it being short yardage situation there, a gap could pop like that and that's happened. We're proud of AP, but ultimately the guys up front also."

Peterson's third touchdown, coupled with an ensuing two-point conversion, sealed a 31-24 victory, improving UTSA to 26-1 against conference opponents under Traylor in the Alamodome.

South Florida took a 24-23 lead with 1:56 remaining on a touchdown connection from Michael Van Buren Jr. to D.J. Crowther. UTSA responded with one of the more unconventional two-minute drills in recent memory. The Roadrunners netted just five yards on three passing attempts, instead leaning on a ground game that produced 70 yards on seven carries. Two of those plays — including a critical 3rd-and-5 conversion — were designed passing plays on which McCown found daylight and scrambled for significant pickups. Another was a 26-yard scamper by Will Henderson III that brought UTSA to the 1-yard line, setting the stage for Peterson's game-winning score.

"We knew they were going to mix up a bunch of different coverages, so it wasn't so much about what they were doing. It's just executing the plays that were called," McCown said on the approach to the final drive. "I thought Coach (Rick) Bowie did a great job really timing when to run the ball, because there were such light boxes. You know, those safeties and DBs are out there thinking it's a bunch of pass."

Late-game execution has become a defining feature of this UTSA team. The Roadrunners were involved in a one-score game in the fourth quarter for the fourth time this year, and they improved to 4-0 in such contests. Four weeks earlier at Texas State, UTSA delivered similar late-game heroics while trailing in the final two minutes, with McCown leading the charge.

"Yeah, kid is special. I'm glad y'all get to see him healthy," Traylor said of McCown. "I wish I could have seen him that way all last year. He took a lot of unnecessary flack, and I'm glad he's healthy… Kid is just special. Some of it was design, some of that was just effort, and some of that was just guts. When you've got a great quarterback, man, you always got a chance."

UTSA finished with 277 rushing yards, nearly matching South Florida's 288 total yards of offense. Peterson led the way with 92 yards, Henderson added 86, and McCown chipped in 52 — his highest rushing total in his last 17 starts.

"Just trying to be the athlete I am," McCown said of his success running the football. "Once again, being healthy helps a ton. So just if it calls for me to go scramble and make a play, then that's what I've been coached to do and that's what I will go do."

South Florida's offense had sputtered through the opening halves of its first four games against FBS competition, scoring just 16 first half points in the form of one touchdown and three field goals. But the Bulls came out firing in the Alamodome, putting up 14 points in the opening quarter. Crowther concluded a successful opening drive with a 15-yard touchdown run, and Bryson Rodgers later sprinted past the UTSA defense to haul in a 42-yard bomb from Van Buren.

"We've got to do a better job of keeping that momentum," Van Buren said. "At the end of the day, that's our standard. To be able to play to our standard, we have to sustain our standard. It all starts with me, and just being able to stay on the field and make the routine routine."

That first quarter offensive momentum would later subside. From the start of the second quarter until after the two-minute timeout in the fourth, UTSA held USF to a mere field goal. The Roadrunner defense didn't even need turnovers to swing the momentum. Instead, they relied on consistent stops, even after leading tackler Brandon Tucker Jr. was ejected in the first half for targeting. In Tucker's absence, defensive end Jeremiah Bailey overwhelmed the Bulls' offensive line with consistent pressure, while outside linebacker Owen Pewee recorded a team-high eight tackles to stifle South Florida's run game.

"Everybody was up. Everybody was hype. Everybody was cheering for each other. Everybody was talking to each other, making sure we encourage each other to keep going," Pewee said of the defense's second half response. "The score is 0-0 coming out of halftime. That's our mentality, so we just got to go out there and just prove it."

The offense capitalized on that defensive succcess. UTSA trailed 17-10 at halftime but scored on all four of its second half possessions to secure its fifth victory of the season — and its second while trailing in the fourth quarter.

"You could just tell at halftime. I keep telling y'all this. The measure of a man or woman is, where are you at a time of crisis?" Traylor said. "It's easy when you go home and there is money in the account and car's got gas and children aren't crying. Air condition is right at 72. That crap doesn't happen very much in life. Most of the time, car is out of gas, don't have enough money, children are crying, wife is mad, and you got to hang in there. We've been down a lot this year, way too much for my liking. I think we've been behind almost in every freaking game, but we are calm in the moment and our kids listen and they believe every word we tell them and they go out there and execute. You don't get groups like that very much, man. They're just special, special humans."

South Florida (4-2, 1-2 American) was the American's last unbeaten team as recently as the afternoon of Oct. 3, but the Bulls now have two conference losses on their résumé. Despite a heartbreaking defeat in the final minute, head coach Brian Hartline sees signs of progress from his retooled roster. He hopes that growth will soon translate to wins, starting with next week's non-conference finale against Kent State.

"In the end, we are building," Hartline said. "As much as I hate saying that, we are getting better. Just not good enough, fast enough. So, as a group, we need to make sure we're continuing to put in the work to give ourselves a chance. I look forward to the day when the coin turns. But I'm proud of the guys and effort. We're just not consistent enough. There's lots of flashes, just not consistent enough."

UTSA (5-1, 2-0 American) is off to its best start since 2021. The Roadrunners have yet to qualify for the American Championship Game, but they are already showing signs of the resilience required to contend. They've won offensive shootouts. They've won defensive battles. And, most importantly, they've repeatedly found ways to prevail when the games are in balance.

Traylor attributes that to his program's culture.

"If you can get a group to believe — I know it's corny as hell; I sound like Ted Lasso right now — we've got to out-culture people. We've got to beat them with our culture," Traylor said. "Now, you got to have some help. You can't go out there with nothing. But you got to have some help. But you can out-culture people in this new world, and I think we just caught lightning in a bottle… We just got some great freaking kids, man."

articles.title: Teenage figure skaters increasingly targeted by social media abuse as campaign launches
articles.summary: Teenage figure skaters as young as 13 are being increasingly targeted by abusive comments on social media, Olympic gold medalist Evan Bates has warned.In a s...
articles.body:
Teenage figure skaters as young as 13 are being increasingly targeted by abusive comments on social media, Olympic gold medalist Evan Bates has warned.

In a sport which has seen revived popularity since the 2026 Milan Cortina Winter Olympics , Bates said some users were creating "toxic environments" around livestreamed events like Junior Grand Prix figure skating. That's a key event for competitors aged 13 and older with dreams of becoming Olympians in the future.

"We've seen a huge uptick in viewership and our online streams, but with that comes more chatter and unfortunately more of that negativity," said Bates, who chairs the International Skating Union's athletes committee.

"We're talking about minors and kids who don't deserve that kind of abuse. A skater's pursuit of their dream to skate at ISU level shouldn't come at the expense of their mental health or well-being."

Bates was speaking ahead of the International Skating Union signing up Friday to a campaign against online abuse. The ISU, which runs figure skating and speedskating, has also pledged to extend a program giving competitors access to AI-powered software which can hide abusive comments on their social media accounts from view.

Bates and his ice dance partner Madison Chock are two of the most experienced and decorated athletes in the sport. The 37-year-old American said he wanted to see other high-profile skaters be more vocal when they see online abuse.

"More and more I'd love to see these athletes, these older athletes who've been through it, step forward and call out people who are creating these kind of toxic environments for skaters," he said.

In an unusual meeting of skating and auto racing, the ISU has signed up to the United Against Online Abuse campaign. That was originally set up by auto racing body the FIA, whose own sport has increasingly seen on-track rivalries mirrored by social-media hostility .

Bates said he's trying to recruit skaters to use a tool he likened to a "shield" which blocks abusive or negative posts from view on their social media despite a "natural hesitance" to allow a third-party tool access to their accounts.

He said the tool has flagged up 300,000 "negative comments," half of them during the Olympics, on the accounts of 92 skaters using the system.

"I think to a certain extent it is internet culture. I don't think it's new. Harassment and abuse of athletes isn't new," Bates said. "As a soccer fan or a football fan, NBA fan, it's sometimes crazy to hear the things that even people in the stadium shout at the players on the field. I think now there's just a means to reaching athletes through social media that's more direct."

articles.title: Caitlin Clark wants Kelsey Mitchell to be with Indiana Fever for life: 'We need her'
articles.summary: Caitlin Clark declared her stance on Kelsey Mitchell's future in no uncertain terms: "I hope I get to play alongside her for the rest of my career."
articles.body:
INDIANAPOLIS — Kelsey Mitchell will be the first domino to fall in the Indiana Fever offseason.

An unrestricted free agent for the first time in her career, the 30-year-old guard became the franchise's first $1 million player in April and following her historic 2026 campaign , she will command a similar salary with her next contract — likely with a longer term.

The Fever have seven players under contract for 2027 and are projected to have approximately $3.6 million in cap space to play with, according to Spotrac.

Once a decision is made on Mitchell's future, the front office can move forward with negotiating a possible EPIC extension with superstar Caitlin Clark and shoring up specific position groups (i.e. frontcourt and wing).

Indiana Fever All-Star Kelsey Mitchell is having an MVP-caliber season

General manager Amber Cox said Saturday that keeping the big three of Mitchell, Clark and center Aliyah Boston together is "a priority."

Coach Stephanie White referred to-resigning Mitchell as Indiana's No. 1 priority, first in the aftermath of the team's Game 3 loss to Las Vegas , then again during her end-of-season news conference.

And on Thursday, Clark declared her stance on Mitchell's future in no uncertain terms: "I hope I get to play alongside Kelsey for the rest of my career. … There's nobody I would rather share the backcourt with other than her."

The second pair to average over 20 points per game apiece in WNBA history (forward Diana Taurasi and guard Cappie Pondexter, 2008), the historically prolific pairing of Mitchell and Clark generated a combined 47 points per game for an offense that averaged 96 points as a unit.

The All-WNBA first team honorees made it all look effortless, demonstrating a unique chemistry as they both displayed their individual scoring prowess.

The two have texted since the season ended, Clark said, wrapping up the season and, from her side, expressing her appreciation for Mitchell.

"Kelsey's always had my back and always appreciated my game," Clark said. "She's always said a lot of really positive things about me as an individual and a basketball player. … She's lifted me up in what I can provide to this organization and the way I've been able to perform, and I'd like to think I've been able to help her and help uplift her game, too, and show the world how great a person she is and great player she is."

The opportunity to run it back with Clark and Boston may incentivize a return to Indy for Mitchell, but make no mistake, she will be paid regardless of where she goes.

The 2018 Ohio State grad averaged a career-high 24.7 points on a career-best 50.9% shooting (45% from 3, also a new high-water mark). She set the single-season scoring record with 1,086 points and constructed a record-setting run of 27 consecutive games with at least 20 points .

"I often tell her, 'I feel like I have the best seat in the house every single night, because I get to watch you do your thing and be right next to you,'" Clark said.

"This organization and these fans have really rallied around her and have supported her," she said. "More than anything, I hope she comes back here and the arena is chanting 'M-V-P' for her again, because that's what she deserves."

The question will be how the Fever navigate the salary cap.

Boston's supermax deal will pay her 22.14% of the cap beginning next season (salary projected at $1.55 million) and a potential EPIC extension for Clark could pay her up to 17% of the cap — though she was noncommittal Thursday on if she would sign an such a deal in an effort to maintain cap space .

Navigating cap constraints while building a roster capable of competing for championships is a challenge for Cox and the Fever front office.

For Clark — and the rest of the Indiana Fever players under contract — it's all hands on deck for Mitchell's recruitment.

"We're gonna work our butt off to get her back. We're going to recruit her as hard as we can," Clark said. "We need her. We love her. … I've shared with Kelsey how much I really want her back and how much I would love to continue playing with her. Hopefully we can keep her here for the rest of her career."

articles.title: Caitlin Clark wants Kelsey Mitchell to be with Indiana Fever for life: 'We need her'
articles.summary: Caitlin Clark declared her stance on Kelsey Mitchell's future in no uncertain terms: "I hope I get to play alongside her for the rest of my career."
articles.body:
INDIANAPOLIS — Kelsey Mitchell will be the first domino to fall in the Indiana Fever offseason.

An unrestricted free agent for the first time in her career, the 30-year-old guard became the franchise's first $1 million player in April and following her historic 2026 campaign , she will command a similar salary with her next contract — likely with a longer term.

The Fever have seven players under contract for 2027 and are projected to have approximately $3.6 million in cap space to play with, according to Spotrac.

Once a decision is made on Mitchell's future, the front office can move forward with negotiating a possible EPIC extension with superstar Caitlin Clark and shoring up specific position groups (i.e. frontcourt and wing).

Indiana Fever All-Star Kelsey Mitchell is having an MVP-caliber season

General manager Amber Cox said Saturday that keeping the big three of Mitchell, Clark and center Aliyah Boston together is "a priority."

Coach Stephanie White referred to-resigning Mitchell as Indiana's No. 1 priority, first in the aftermath of the team's Game 3 loss to Las Vegas , then again during her end-of-season news conference.

And on Thursday, Clark declared her stance on Mitchell's future in no uncertain terms: "I hope I get to play alongside Kelsey for the rest of my career. … There's nobody I would rather share the backcourt with other than her."

The second pair to average over 20 points per game apiece in WNBA history (forward Diana Taurasi and guard Cappie Pondexter, 2008), the historically prolific pairing of Mitchell and Clark generated a combined 47 points per game for an offense that averaged 96 points as a unit.

The All-WNBA first team honorees made it all look effortless, demonstrating a unique chemistry as they both displayed their individual scoring prowess.

The two have texted since the season ended, Clark said, wrapping up the season and, from her side, expressing her appreciation for Mitchell.

"Kelsey's always had my back and always appreciated my game," Clark said. "She's always said a lot of really positive things about me as an individual and a basketball player. … She's lifted me up in what I can provide to this organization and the way I've been able to perform, and I'd like to think I've been able to help her and help uplift her game, too, and show the world how great a person she is and great player she is."

The opportunity to run it back with Clark and Boston may incentivize a return to Indy for Mitchell, but make no mistake, she will be paid regardless of where she goes.

The 2018 Ohio State grad averaged a career-high 24.7 points on a career-best 50.9% shooting (45% from 3, also a new high-water mark). She set the single-season scoring record with 1,086 points and constructed a record-setting run of 27 consecutive games with at least 20 points .

"I often tell her, 'I feel like I have the best seat in the house every single night, because I get to watch you do your thing and be right next to you,'" Clark said.

"This organization and these fans have really rallied around her and have supported her," she said. "More than anything, I hope she comes back here and the arena is chanting 'M-V-P' for her again, because that's what she deserves."

The question will be how the Fever navigate the salary cap.

Boston's supermax deal will pay her 22.14% of the cap beginning next season (salary projected at $1.55 million) and a potential EPIC extension for Clark could pay her up to 17% of the cap — though she was noncommittal Thursday on if she would sign an such a deal in an effort to maintain cap space .

Navigating cap constraints while building a roster capable of competing for championships is a challenge for Cox and the Fever front office.

For Clark — and the rest of the Indiana Fever players under contract — it's all hands on deck for Mitchell's recruitment.

"We're gonna work our butt off to get her back. We're going to recruit her as hard as we can," Clark said. "We need her. We love her. … I've shared with Kelsey how much I really want her back and how much I would love to continue playing with her. Hopefully we can keep her here for the rest of her career."

articles.title: MotoGP Indonesian Grand Prix: Raul Fernandez on top as Aprilia dominates
articles.summary: All the title contenders made Q2 at Mandalika, but Fernandez looks to have found his best form
articles.body:
Aprilia lived up to expectations at Mandalika on Friday, with Raul Fernandez breaking the lap record to lead a 1-2-3 for the Italian marque in Practice.

Only the factory riders, Marco Bezzecchi and Jorge Martin, were able to get within half a second of the Trackhouse rider, who was consistently fast throughout the day on the island of Lombok.

Pedro Acosta (KTM) and Marc Marquez (Ducati) booked their tickets into Qualifying 2 with fourth and fifth places respectively, ensuring the top four in the championship will be in the Q2 mix. But both have a considerable lap time deficit to ponder.

Fabio Di Giannantonio (VR46 Ducati) was sixth-fastest, with team-mate Franco Morbidelli joining him in Q2 with ninth spot.

Fabio Quartararo wowed onlookers by delivering the seventh-fastest time despite a violent tumble through the gravel midway through the session. He limped away from the fall and spent a few minutes nursing his left wrist in the factory Yamaha garage before emerging to improve his time and book his passage to Q2.

Alex Marquez (Gresini Ducati) was lucky to remain in the top 10 despite crashing with a couple of minutes remaining. The resulting yellow flags may have helped his cause, as did those produced by late falls for Alex Rins (Yamaha) and Enea Bastianini (Tech3 KTM).

Francesco Bagnaia dodged the yellows on the second factory Ducati to sneak into tenth spot at the very end of the session.

2025 Indonesian Grand Prix winner Fermin Aldeguer endured a nightmare day that included a crash in the morning, another crash early in the Practice session and then an apparent technical issue just when it was time to push for laps. Unsurprisingly, the Gresini rider was unable to trouble the top 10 and may struggle to repeat his 2025 exploits from there.

The only Aprilia not flying on Friday was the Trackhouse entry of Ai Ogura, who fell in the morning and was unable to find both speed and a clear track at the same moment. He'll be joined in Q1 by Bastianini, who racked up two falls in the afternoon session and will have to work hard to deliver another weekend like he did in Japan last time out.

articles.title: UTSA recaptures comeback magic, rallying to beat USF in final minute
articles.summary: The Roadrunners have faced four tight finishes in 2026 and have emerged with four wins, sparking memories of past seasons that ended in championships.
articles.body:
As UTSA coach Jeff Traylor was guiding the program's rise to Conference USA championships in 2021 and 2022, he often fell back on a familiar motto: "A champion has the ability to play one play longer than the opponent."

Through his first three seasons, UTSA proved him right week after week, going 18-7 in games that were within a one-score margin at any point during the fourth quarter.

As UTSA slipped back to earth with 7-6 records the past two seasons, that magic often seemed to be lost, as the Roadrunners went just 2-6 in games that were decided by one score.

But when he stepped into the locker room at halftime facing yet another deficit Thursday against South Florida, Traylor could sense a different reaction from a roster that was built by prioritizing maturity and composure over talent and athleticism.

This UTSA group is one "you're going to have to kill," Traylor said, and after USF scored with less than two minutes remaining to take a lead, the Roadrunners proved him right yet again.

UTSA surged down the field behind explosive runs from Owen McCown and Will Henderson, setting up A'Marion Peterson for his third rushing touchdown of the game with 15 seconds remaining to spur a 31-24 win against USF on Thursday in the Alamodome.

"We're calm in the moment, and our kids listen," Traylor said. "You can tell they really believe every word we tell them, and they go out there and execute. You don't get groups like that very much, man. They're just special, special humans."

All four of UTSA's games against Group of Six competition this year have been played within a one-score margin in the final quarter, and all four have ended in Roadrunners' wins.

Thursday's victory continues UTSA's best start since 2021, as the Roadrunners moved to 5-1 and 2-0 in the American Conference. UTSA also improved to 36-5 in the Alamodome under Traylor, including a 26-1 mark against conference opponents.

UTSA found a way Thursday against a South Florida team that reportedly spent close to the $20 million revenue sharing cap to rebuild its roster, boasting a payroll about four to five times UTSA's total.

But Traylor sees a formula to close the gap with the "Triangle of Toughness" culture he's preached since day one, meshed with this year's new mantra "Ubuntu," meaning "I am because we are."

He understands how cliche the whole thing sounds, but he believes every word.

"It's going to give us a fighting chance," Traylor said. "In the new rev share era where everybody's about getting another agent, getting more money and getting out. If you can get a group to believe - and I know it's corny as hell, I sound like Ted Lasso right now - we've got to out-culture people. We've got to beat them with our culture."

Facing a 17-10 deficit at halftime, UTSA's offense came alive with scores on all four second-half drives, sustaining long series to hold the ball for nearly 20 minutes. The Roadrunners outgained the Bulls 271-87 after halftime and finished with 277 total rushing yards to mark the highest total since 2024.

The Roadrunners' defense held the Bulls to 15 yards and a pair of punts to open the half, but USF found one final push. The Bulls drove 75 yards over more than six minutes to set up an 11-yard touchdown pass from Michael Van Buren to DJ Crowther, going up 24-23 with less than two minutes to play.

As the Roadrunners retook the field, McCown said the group exchanged knowing nods in place of any kind of pep talk, having already come through in a similar situation this year with a last-minute touchdown to beat Texas State.

McCown sparked the series with a 19-yard scramble on third-and-5, showing off the rushing ability that was dormant as he played through injury last year. He finished the game 22-of-31 passing for 209 yards and added a season-high 52 yards on the ground.

"Man, I feel super great, super healthy," McCown said. "To be able to be myself like I know I can be, and the athlete that I am, is super comforting."

Henderson followed with a 26-yard burst to move the ball to the 1-yard line, and Peterson punched in the score with a direct snap play out of a jumbo package that accounted for all three UTSA touchdowns.

As the Roadrunners sealed the win, senior linebacker Owen Pewee said he was reminded of the 2022 championship team he played on as a true freshman, seeing a group that trusts in each other to deliver.

"I feel like we're made for this," Pewee said. "This is a different team this year, so I feel like it was going to be good. We had a lot of confidence going into this game."

With only a few days to prepare for Thursday's kickoff following Saturday's 16-14 win at Rice, Traylor kept the group out of pads in practice this week, holding light walkthroughs. UTSA found all the necessary motivation from USF coach Brian Hartline, who on Monday raised old questions about the authenticity of the Alamodome's crowd noise .

Traylor made sure the Roadrunners heard every word, understanding the message the comments send about the program UTSA has built.

"My former players take it as a challenge for everything we've done here. It's all been bogus," Traylor said. "It's almost like they're telling us we don't deserve that. That's how we take that."

Traylor said some of the Roadrunners were disappointed to see so many empty seats in the announced crowd of 17,632, though he also noted the students in particular "showed up and showed out," creating a loud atmosphere.

Entering a long week of preparation for another home matchup against Navy at 7 p.m. on Oct. 17, Traylor described the Roadrunners as "not even good yet," with plenty of areas still to iron out. He expects the fan support to continue improving right along with them.

"I had some kids that were pretty upset, not mad at anybody, but they like to play in front of a big crowd," Traylor said. "I told them, 'Win tonight, and watch the city get hopping at seven o'clock next Saturday night.'"

articles.title: South Carolina football vs Florida prediction. Can Shane Beamer end SEC losing streak?
articles.summary: South Carolina football plays Florida in Week 6 of the 2026 season. See our picks and predictions.
articles.body:
South Carolina football is in desperate need of a win.

Coach Shane Beamer hasn't beaten an SEC team since September 2025 and his losing streak was extended to eight straight conference games with a 35-34 overtime loss to Kentucky .

Now the Gamecocks (2-3, 0-3 SEC) play at No. 15 Florida (4-1, 2-1) on Oct. 10 (12:45 p.m. ET, SEC Network), which is coming off a 45-17 loss to Missouri.

Here's The Greenville News' prediction on how the game will go.

South Carolina football vs Kentucky, Shane Beamer, LaNorris Sellers, Kenny Minchey photos

Florida looked like a completely different team in Week 4 when it beat Ole Miss 52-28 than it did when it lost to Missouri. South Carolina has looked somewhat consistent in SEC play but not in a good way.

The Gamecocks led by 16 and 17 before going on to lose vs Mississippi State and Kentucky, respectively.

Both teams started the season with easy wins before Florida picked up two straight to begin conference play in Year 1 under coach Jon Sumrall.

With rain in the forecast, it's likely going to be a run heavy game and will come down to who can dominate on the ground. Lucky for South Carolina, it's secondary has been its weakness and is allowing the sixth-fewest rushing yards in per game in the SEC right now.

That said, with the anger and embarrassment from last week's drubbing still on Florida's mind, the Gators will outplay South Carolina, pulling away in the fourth quarter.

South Carolina vs Florida scouting report

Why South Carolina has an advantage : The Gamecocks are the underdogs and it's a road game so they could knock Florida off its game early unexpectedly.

Quarterback LaNorris Sellers is coming off his best game of the season where he went 20-of-36 for 226 passing yards with two touchdowns and 147 rushing yards. That could give him confidence. Florida quarterback Aaron Philo completed a season-low 61.8% of his passes and was sacked three times last week.

South Carolina is averaging an SEC-best 256 rushing yards per game (199 ypg in SEC games) led by Matt Fuller, who has 433 rushing yards.

Missouri held the Gators to 42 rushing yards after they ran for a combined 545 yards in their first two SEC games against the two worst rushing defenses in the SEC. Like Missouri, South Carolina should have a better chance at stopping the run.

Why Florida has an advantage : Despite last week's rushing struggles, Florida has Jadan Baugh, who has 613 rushing yards, the fifth most in the country.

Philo has also only thrown two interceptions compared to eight touchdowns.

South Carolina's secondary is struggling and has had busts in coverage the last three games, which gives the Gators more opportunities on offense beyond just Baugh. South Carolina star wide receiver Nyck Harbor has been a non-factor so he's less of a worry on defense for Florida, and other Gamecocks receivers have struggled with dropping the ball.

Dallas Wilson has a team-high 302 receiving yards and three touchdowns for Florida.

Since 2022, Beamer's teams have led by 10 or more points and went on to lose the game seven times, which means Florida should feel comfortable even if it's down by two touchdowns at any point in the game.

South Carolina vs Florida score prediction

Florida 28: South Carolina 21 : Florida showed some flaws vs Missouri after looking unbeatable vs Ole Miss. But the Gamecocks continue to find ways to beat themselves, whether that's failed fourth-down conversions, coverage busts or red zone stalls. This game stays close but the Gators refuse to lose two straight, scoring midway through the fourth quarter to take the win.

articles.title: Ryan Hall: Leeds Rhinos wing retires from rugby league after storied 20-year career
articles.summary: Ryan Hall made over 500 career appearances and scored 275 Super League tries, second only to current Leigh winger Josh Charnley; the 38-year-old made his Leeds Rhinos debut in 2007, going on to win six Super League titles with the club
articles.body:
The 38-year-old made his Rhinos debut in 2007 and went on to win six Super League titles with the club before helping Hull KR reach Old Trafford in 2024.

He made over 500 career appearances and scored 275 Super League tries, second only to current Leigh winger Josh Charnley in the league's all-time list.

Hall will be granted a three-month testimonial period from December, including one final appearance in a friendly against Hull FC, before taking up a commercial role at Headingley.

Upon his announcement on Friday, Hall said: "I'm officially retiring from playing rugby league.

"I think the time's right that I hang up the boots. I've done it for 20 years and I've loved every minute of it.

"The club's in a good position to go with the youth, that's the natural progression in rugby league. I've always wanted the best for the club at heart and if the decision is to go with the youth at this point in time, that suits me down to a tee because I have had 20 years of loving every second of it."

Hall had a disappointing two-year spell with Sydney Roosters in the NRL after his first stint with Rhinos ended in 2018. He signed with Hull KR ahead of the 2021 season, before returning to Leeds in 2024.

He was capped 40 times for England, scoring 39 tries, and twice for Great Britain on the 2019 Lions tour of the southern hemisphere.
